findings.claim: Tier 2 (M5, the 11/12 Ozluk de-conditionalization) is presented as requiring dispersion technology 'to be built', but its key arithmetic largely exists in uncited literature (Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill ~2014; Montgomery-Hooley Barban-Davenport-Halberstam asymptotics), which simultaneously raises tractability and lowers the novelty of the proposal's strongest claimed 'first'.
findings.argument: The proposal's failure-mode section flags Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan but misses the closest paper: Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill, 'Simple zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions and the asymptotic large sieve' (~2014), which already carried out exactly 'Ozluk's 11/12 via support-2 family form factor', with the moment/large-sieve computation done and GRH used only in the zero-side conversion (Montgomery's argument needs zeros on the line to convert form-factor data into simplicity). Since the Zeta23 rank-trace zero side is precisely a GRH-free replacement for that conversion, M5 = CLLR arithmetic + existing formalized zero side — likely substantially easier than the '18-30+ months horizon with dispersion wall' pricing. Separately, the (1,2)-band family form factor after q-averaging is classically tied to the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam variance: the Montgomery (1970)/Hooley asymptotic sum_{q<=Q} sum_a* (psi(x;q,a) - x/phi(q))^2 ~ Qx log Q - cQx holds unconditionally for Q >= x^{1/2+eps}, i.e. exactly X <= Q^{2-eps}, the proposal's claimed range; the variance <-> form-factor dictionary is classical (Friedlander-Goldston, Goldston-Vaughan). Consequences: (a) the 'Tier 2 dispersion wall' failure mode may be vacuous below Lambda = 2-eps; (b) the novelty claims 'no unconditional result above 2/3 in ANY family' and 'the dispersion technology gets built here' must be re-positioned — the de-conditionalization itself appears genuinely unclaimed (CLLR's simplicity statement is GRH-conditional), but the proposal is consuming, not building, the hard arithmetic; (c) the by-product 'AH refuted on family average' loses some luster since Ozluk 1996 already refuted it under GRH, and family-averaged bandwidth-2 data says nothing about AH for zeta itself (which the proposal's own honesty section concedes). Repair: cite and position against CLLR and Montgomery-Hooley explicitly; consider promoting a partial-range M5 (Lambda = 1+c via BDH variance) to an earlier milestone, since kappa_fam(1.5) = 1.1481 gives 0.8519 on average — already above the 0.8453 two-moment all-bandwidth cap, a headline in itself.

findings.claim: F1's 'STATUS OF INPUTS' line — 'per-character explicit formula, zero-side block decomposition, Lemma R, and assembly - all proven AND formalized (ThmE pipeline)' — overstates what exists: both the paper's Theorem E and the Lean ThmE are fixed-q, and the q-uniformity that constitutes essentially all of F1's real labor is nowhere proven.
findings.argument: The condensed map states explicitly: 'Theorem E is for FIXED primitive chi mod q > 1 (constants and T0 depend on q; no q-uniformity is claimed), so no application to q-aspect problems as formalized.' Every error field (E_T, tail thresholds, RvM constants, CrossMuP bounds) must be re-derived with constants tracked jointly in (q,T) in the regime T = polylog(q), where the paper's own engineering (Section 5 designed for T -> infinity at fixed lambda) is being used far outside its design envelope. The proposal knows this — the Lean hook says 'this code with q-uniform error tracking' and failure mode 2 prices it — but the F1 statement's input-status wording would mislead a reader into thinking only orthogonality and the taper are new. This matters for confidence calibration: the designer's 0.8 is about right for the paper-side theorem (I estimate 0.75-0.85 for a strong group in 2 years — the mathematics is one classical-analysis lemma plus laborious uniform re-running of a published pipeline plus exact orthogonality), but a Lean-inclusive F1 is more like 0.6, because the uniformity discipline must be rebuilt formally, not just re-checked.

findings.claim: The dual-term bound in the Tier-1 second moment ('bounded trivially by L^2 X/q') is stated without the divisor-counting step it actually needs, and the Ingham criterion is quoted in a nonstandard normalization; both are repairable but a referee of the eventual paper will stop at each.
findings.argument: The chi(n)chi(m) terms force nm == 1 (mod q), nm <= X^2, with n,m prime powers weighted Lambda(n)Lambda(m)/sqrt(nm). Writing nm = 1 + jq, the sum is <= L^2 sum_{1<=j<=X^2/q} r_2(1+jq)/sqrt(jq), where r_2(k) counts ordered factorizations of k into two prime powers; r_2 is divisor-bounded but not O(1), so the clean bound is L^2 (X/q) x (small divisor factor), not literally L^2 X/q; also j=0 (nm=1) is void since Lambda(1)=0. The bound survives with room to spare (Lambda <= 1 - 1/loglog q gives X/q <= e^{-log q/loglog q}), so this is bookkeeping, not a gap. On the taper: Ingham's 1934 criterion for a compactly supported function with |phihat(r)| <= exp(-eps(|r|)) is integral eps(t)/t^2 dt < infinity (absolute-decay normalization); the proposal writes 'integral of eps(t)/t dt < infinity' which is correct only in the relative normalization exp(-|r| eps(|r|)) with eps(r) = c/(log r)^{1+delta}. The two are equivalent here, and I verified the product-of-sincs construction does deliver log(1/|phihat(r)|) >> r/(log r)^{1+delta} (number of active factors J ~ c r/(log r)^{1+delta}, each contributing ~ a constant on average) with L-INDEPENDENT constants since the total taper width w = 1 is fixed — so failure mode 1 (crossover radius r0 growing with L) is actually overly pessimistic: only the (L-w)-sinc factor depends on L and it contributes type, not decay rate. The T0 tail arithmetic checks out: need c T/(loglog q)^{2+delta} >= (Lambda/2 + 1) log q, satisfied for T >= (log q)^{1+delta'} at large q.

findings.claim: The Lean cost of M1 is understated: 'Poisson.lean already accepts it' is true for the Gabor-Poisson identity, but the tail/summability chain is formalized in the (1+|r|)^{-2} currency from compact support + C^2, and the whole point of T0 is to replace that currency — new formal analysis, including an infinite convolution product, is required.
findings.argument: Per the map, 'the explicit formula is formalized ONLY for C_c^2 test functions' (fine: the Ingham taper is C-infinity with exact compact support) and 'ZeroSummability gives absolute convergence only via (1+|r|)^{-2} decay from compact support + C^2'. The F1 pipeline needs the tail estimate rebuilt with the near-exponential T0 decay as the summability input, uniformly in (q,T) — a new lemma chain, not a plug-in. Moreover phihat is an infinite product of sincs; formalizing its strip bound requires handling the infinite convolution (convergence of the product, uniform bounds, evenness, the 'phi = 1 on the middle' property) in Mathlib — standard mathematics but a real formalization project, plausibly comparable in size to the claimed '3-5 page' paper lemma times the usual Lean multiplier. This does not threaten M1's feasibility (months 0-4 is tight but possible for the paper version; the simultaneous Lean claim is optimistic), and option (b) in the Lean hook (the five-line direct-sum certificate lemma) is correctly identified as the genuinely cheap first formal artifact.

findings.claim: Novelty items (4) and (5) are inflated: the 'direct-sum organizing principle' is a repackaging of Remark 7.2(iii)'s linearity observation, and the GL(2) 'first' must be positioned against existing GL(2) critical-line results reached by other methods.
findings.argument: The map records, in three independent readings of the anchor artifact, the sentence 'Lemma 3.2 is linear in tr and ||.||_F^2, so both commute with averaging over families; orthogonality of characters restores Lambda* = 1... promising 2/3 on the line on average over chi mod q with T as small as a power of log q. Missing ingredient... Gevrey-class taper. Concrete, unstarted project.' So the core mechanism, the operating regime, the expected constant, AND the missing lemma are all the anchor paper's own; the proposal's genuine additions are the explicit taper design, the uniform-error execution plan, Tier 2, M3/M4, and the numerics — a 'carry out the named hook' proposal, which its Novelty section does acknowledge in item (1) but then partially re-claims in item (4) ('new as an organizing principle': block-diagonal additivity of tr/Frobenius/rank/n_+ is a triviality once linearity is observed). For M4: Hafner (Math. Ann. 1983) proved a positive proportion of zeros of cusp-form L-functions on the critical line, and Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2508.11108, already in the program's own literature file) 'more than doubles critical-line proportions for GL(2)'; the proposal's method-qualified phrasing ('by ANY variant of this method') is defensible, and 2/3-simple-on-average at polylog height would genuinely exceed anything known for GL(2), but a published version claiming 'first nonvacuous' without these citations would be refereed harshly. Similarly, the 'first proportion theorem at polylog height in any family' claim should be delimited against the one-level-density literature (Hughes-Rudnick 2003, Ozluk-Snyder), which operates at the central-point scale ~1/log q — a different regime, so the claim likely stands, but the boundary must be drawn explicitly.

findings.claim: The obstruction-canon handling is correct and unusually honest — in particular the escape from the '0.845 at any bandwidth' cap is legitimate — but the proposal's zeta-facing value should be scored as zero direct content plus technology transfer only, per its own admission.
findings.argument: I verified the key evasion computation: the formalized cap 2 - kappa(lambda) <= 2 - 2/sqrt(3) = 0.8453 is a corollary of the specific formula kappa(lambda) = 1/lambda + lambda/3, i.e. form factor |alpha| at ALL frequencies; with the family plateau F = 1 on (1, Lambda) the second-moment constant is kappa_fam(Lambda) = 1/Lambda + (Lambda - 2/3 + (Lambda-1)^2)/Lambda^2 (I re-derived the integral: 2[int_0^1 (Lambda-a)a da + int_1^Lambda (Lambda-a) da] = Lambda - 2/3 + (Lambda-1)^2, confirmed numerically), giving 13/12 at Lambda = 2 and hence 11/12 — no formalized theorem is contradicted since count_certificate is parametric in kappa, and the PairCeiling scope note explicitly lists family averaging and bandwidth > 1 as outside the ceiling. Tier 1 stays below 0.6818 so nothing is claimed there either. The DH/Epstein, dimension-cap, lemmaR_tight, parity, Rodgers-Tao, Bombieri-Garrett, and Conrey-Li entries are all handled correctly, and the proposal states outright that no sub-direction yields a zeta statement beyond 2/3 ('an off-line zero of one L(s,chi)... cannot influence another summand' — correct: block-diagonality forecloses any Deuring-Heilbronn-type repulsion inside a two-moment certificate). The residual zeta claim — that Tier 2 'battle-tests' the averaged shifted-convolution technology whose t-aspect analogue is the named door past 0.6818 — is real but weaker than it sounds: the t-aspect analogue (averaged Hardy-Littlewood in the SHIFT variable at fixed modulus structure) is a materially different and harder averaging than averaging over moduli q, so transfer is aspirational. Scored accordingly: this is a proportions machine for families, valuable as such, with zero direct RH content — exactly as the proposal itself says.

verdicts.repairs: (1) Cite and position against Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill (~2014, asymptotic large sieve + GRH -> 11/12 simple for primitive Dirichlet L) and the Montgomery-Hooley Barban-Davenport-Halberstam asymptotic (unconditional for Q >= x^{1/2+eps}): re-scope M5 as 'de-conditionalize CLLR' rather than 'build dispersion technology', and consider promoting a partial-range Lambda = 1+c theorem (via BDH variance; kappa_fam(1.5) = 1.1481 already certifies 0.8519 > 0.8453) to a nearer milestone. (2) Reword F1's STATUS OF INPUTS: the ThmE pipeline (paper and Lean) is fixed-q; state that all q-uniformity is new work, matching what the Lean-hook section already admits. (3) Fix the two small technical statements: the dual-term bound needs the divisor-counting step (sum over nm = 1 + jq of ordered prime-power factorizations, r_2 divisor-bounded), and the Ingham criterion should be quoted in the standard normalization (integral eps(t)/t^2 dt < infinity for absolute decay exp(-eps(|r|))). (4) Budget the Lean tail-chain rework honestly: ZeroSummability's (1+|r|)^{-2} currency must be re-proven with T0 decay, and the infinite sinc product formalized; decouple M1's paper deadline from its Lean deadline, and lead with the cheap direct-sum certificate lemma as the first formal artifact. (5) Delimit the 'first at polylog height' and GL(2) 'first' claims against Hughes-Rudnick/Ozluk-Snyder central-point-scale density results, Hafner 1983, and arXiv:2508.11108. (6) Drop or demote novelty item (4) (direct-sum framing) to an expository convenience.
literature_flags: Chandee-Lee-Liu-Radziwill (~2014), 'Simple zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions and the asymptotic large sieve' — the closest existing paper to M5 (11/12 simple under GRH via support-2 family form factor); NOT cited in the proposal; must be verified and positioned against before any 'first'/'no unconditional result above 2/3 in any family' claim.

Ozluk, J. Number Theory 59 (1996) — q-averaged form factor on |alpha| < 2 under GRH and the 11/12 simplicity consequence; proposal recalls it correctly as far as I can tell, but the exact statement (aggregate vs primitive characters, height ranges, where the simplicity deduction appears — thesis vs paper) needs verification.

Montgomery (1970) / Hooley — Barban-Davenport-Halberstam variance asymptotics, unconditional range Q >= x^{1/2+eps}, and the Friedlander-Goldston dictionary between BDH variance and the q-averaged form factor on (1,2): if correct, Tier 2's arithmetic in the range Lambda < 2 - eps is classical; needs verification of the exact error terms available at the proposal's tiny-T windowing.

Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan asymptotic large sieve and 'Critical zeros of Dirichlet L-functions' — aggregate critical-line proportion constant (~56-58%, proposal flags it); verify constant and the (q,T) ranges it operates in (whether any polylog-height statement is implicit).
Wu (2019?) q-aspect Levinson ~41.7% per character with log q = o(log T) — recalled from memory in the proposal; verify.

Conrey (1983), zeros of xi^{(k)} on the critical line, proportion -> 1 unconditionally — verify exact statement (on-line vs in-strip, simplicity absent) since sub-direction (ii)'s honesty clause leans on it.

Farmer-Gonek-Lee — pair correlation / second moments for xi' zeros (RH-conditional constants); the k >= 2 'FGL form-factor recursion' the proposal invokes for kappa_k may not exist in print beyond k = 1; verify before M6 claims 'de-conditionalizing FGL beyond k = 1'.

Hafner (Math. Ann. 1983) positive proportion on the line for cusp-form L-functions, and Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh arXiv:2508.11108 (GL(2) proportions doubled) — needed to correctly scope M4's 'first' claim.

Hughes-Rudnick (2003) linear statistics of low-lying zeros for chi mod q (and Ozluk-Snyder for quadratic families) — unconditional support ranges at the central-point scale; needed to delimit the 'first proportion theorem at polylog height in any family' novelty boundary.

Ingham (1934) quasi-analyticity/decay criterion for compactly supported functions — proposal quotes 'integral eps(t)/t dt' (relative-decay normalization); correct in standard form as integral eps(t)/t^2 dt < infinity; the construction itself (product of sincs with widths c/(j (log j)^{1+delta})) is classical and checks out.

Yildirim and other q-aspect pair-correlation work for Dirichlet L-functions — check whether any unconditional (1,2)-band family form-factor statement already exists in print, which would further compress M5's novelty to the certificate conversion alone.

findings.claim: The central asymptotic claim — that for the mu-mollifier the fourth-moment ratio <|B|^4>/<|B|^2>^2 stays O(1) while generic coefficients are log-divergent — is false, and in fact EXACTLY INVERTED; consequently m2 diverges like (theta*log T)^2, the mollified certificate 2*m1^2/m2 - 1 tends to -1 (vacuous) for every fixed theta > 0, and Theorem parts (ii), (iii), (iv) are false as stated.
findings.argument: Write B(s) = sum_{m<=M} b_m m^{-s}, b_m = mu(m)*psi(log(M/m)/log M). The mean fourth moment over tau (valid by Montgomery-Vaughan for M^4 <= T) is <|B|^4> = sum_{n<=M^2} c(n)^2/n with c(n) = sum_{de=n} b_d b_e (Dirichlet self-convolution). KEY SIGN FACT: for squarefree n, mu(d)mu(n/d) = mu(n) for EVERY divisor d, so c(n) = mu(n)*sum_{d|n} psi_d psi_{n/d} — all d(n) terms have the SAME sign; there is no cancellation inside c(n), and |c(n)| ~ d(n) for n in the bulk. Hence sum c(n)^2/n >~ sum_{n<=sqrt(M)} mu^2(n)d(n)^2/n ~ (log M)^4 (the Dirichlet series of (mu*mu)^2 is zeta(s)^4 * H(s), H regular at 1). Meanwhile <|B|^2>^2 = n(b)^2 ~ (c_psi * theta*l)^2 with l = log(T/2pi). So the ratio is ASYMP (log M)^2 = (theta*l)^2 -> infinity. Cross-checks: (a) log-normal heuristic: Var(log|B|) ~ (1/2)loglog M gives <|B|^{2k}> ~ exp(2k^2 Var), ratio = (log M)^2; (b) Gonek's negative-moment analogy: B ~ truncated 1/zeta, and the conjectural (log T)^{k^2} law at k=-2 vs k=-1 gives (log)^4/(log)^2; (c) DIRECT COMPUTATION (run during this review): for b = mu(m)*psi linear profile, the exact ratio sum c(n)^2/n / n(b)^2 at M = 100/300/1000/3000 is 2.149/2.476/2.851/3.209 — monotonically growing with log M — while random +-1 signs on the same squarefree support and profile give 1.66/1.82/1.60/1.91, bounded (-> 2, the complex-Gaussian |Z|^4 = 2(|Z|^2)^2 floor). So the proposal has the comparison backwards: GENERIC coefficients keep the ratio O(1) (square-root cancellation in c(n)); the MOBIUS choice maximizes coherence of b*b (perfectly correlated signs on squarefree n) and is (log M)^2-divergent. The multiplicativity celebrated as 'the analytic shadow of the Euler product' is precisely the mechanism of the blow-up. WHERE IT ENTERS: the proposal itself locates the term correctly — m2's window-Plancherel part is (1/lambda_1)*<|B|^4>-corrected. The kernel Phi(tau-tau')^2 has width ~1/L = 1/(lambda*l) while |B|^2 varies on scale 1/(theta*l) > 1/L for theta < lambda, so |B(tau')|^2 ~ |B(tau)|^2 passes through the Frobenius diagonal UNDAMPED: m2 >= (1/lambda)*<|B|^4>/<|B|^2>^2 ~ (theta*l)^2/lambda. This is a positive square (autocorrelation of |B|^2 at small lag ~ its variance) — it cannot be cancelled by the signed prime-diagonal or cross-diagonal terms, which are O(1) and O(theta*l) respectively. Since m1 = 1 + 2*theta*A-tilde + O(theta^2) = O(1) (that part of the proposal checks out), the certificate 2*m1^2/m2 - 1 -> -1 < 0: asymptotically vacuous, strictly worse than the unmollified 1/2. The stated Theorem (ii) ('m2(b,lambda) + o(1))N' with m2 a T-independent constant) is false for every fixed theta > 0; (iii) then certifies nothing; (iv)'s finite first-variation function G does not exist as claimed — indeed the formula as written, d/dtheta[m1^2/m2] = sum_p (log p/p)G(alpha_p) + o(1), is already internally inconsistent: sum_{p<=T^theta} log p/p ~ theta*log T diverges, so the RHS is l-divergent for any G = O(1) with nonzero integral, a symptom of the missing l-scaling in m2.

findings.claim: Structural kill, robust over ALL coefficient choices: this is a mollifier with nothing to mollify, and no real Dirichlet-polynomial weight b (any length, amplitude, or profile) can improve the two-moment Gram certificate by more than O(1/log T) — so M2/M3's targets (beat 0.6725, beat 0.68183) are unreachable by this route in principle, not just for the mu-choice.
findings.argument: In Levinson/Conrey and CGG/Bui-Heath-Brown, the mollifier multiplies an OSCILLATING object (zeta or zeta'(rho)) and cancels its fluctuations, making the weighted quantity flat: CGG's effective atom weight is |B(rho)zeta'(rho)|^2, engineered to be near-constant, which is why their Cauchy-Schwarz over zeros works. In the Weil-Gram frame the explicit-formula atoms already carry FLAT mass m_rho (there is no zeta'(rho) factor anywhere in the trace); the weight beta_rho = |B(1/2+i*gamma)|^2 alone is the un-mollified reciprocal-zeta-like object. A Cauchy-Schwarz certificate is a Jensen-type functional: zero-side, n_+ >= (sum beta_rho)^2 / (sum beta^2 + cross) <= N^dist with deficit = variance of beta over zeros; ANY non-constant weight is pure cost at leading order, and the only possible profit is the O(theta) correlation bias of beta_rho with zero positions (the Landau-Gonek/trace term). Quantitative pinch (perturbative, b = delta_1 + eps*c, mollifier profile c of length T^theta): m1 gains eps*theta*A_1 (first order, finite — this survives scrutiny; it is the C(b) = Lambda-mu anticorrelation entering the density with a favorable sign); m2 pays eps^2 * c' * theta*l at second order (the variance <|C|^2> ~ theta*l of the perturbation passes undamped through the Plancherel term — see Finding 1 — and at full amplitude grows to (theta*l)^2). Optimizing eps: eps* ~ 1/l, net certificate gain ~ theta/l = O(1/log T) — absorbed into the o(1) of the theorem. The trade-off cannot be engineered away: extracting trace gain of order theta requires <b, T_p b> ~ -n(b) coherently over primes p <= M, i.e. b_{mp} ~ -b_m for all m, p — forcing b toward completely multiplicative Liouville/Mobius-type sign patterns, which is exactly the configuration that makes c = b*b sign-coherent and maximizes the m2 variance cost (Finding 1). Random-like b avoids the (log M)^2 blow-up (ratio -> 2) but then C(b) has square-root cancellation and the trace gain vanishes. Even the residual factor 2 (complex-Gaussian floor: <|B|^4> >= 2<|B|^2>^2(1-o(1)) whenever the polynomial part dominates b_1, i.e. n(b) - 1 >> 1) already turns the lambda=1 certificate from +1/2 into 2/(2+1/3) - 1 < 0. So sup_b [2*m1(b)^2/m2(b) - 1] = unmollified value + O(1/log T): the enlarged invariant family (m1(b), m2(b)) does escape the kappa(lambda) curve, but only on the WRONG side. The proposal's claimed 'new arithmetic quantity outside the kappa curve' is real and useless; the route's engine (multiplicative anticorrelation with Lambda) and its poison (multiplicative coherence of b*b) are the same Euler-product structure.

findings.claim: Regime II (M3, lambda = 1 with theta > 0) mislabels its hard off-diagonal sums: they are Lambda(n)Lambda(m) prime-pair shifted convolutions (Hardy-Littlewood / PCC-for-alpha>1 strength — the canon wall), NOT the divisor-coefficient shifted convolutions of the twisted second moment that Deshouillers-Iwaniec / BCHB / Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill technology evaluates; the claimed technology transfer is a disguised HL prime-pair assumption.
findings.argument: The Gram form's spectral density is |B(1/2+i*tau)|^2 * nu_{X'}(tau), and the oscillating part of nu_X is the EXPLICIT-FORMULA prime polynomial P_X(tau) = sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-i*tau}. The Frobenius norm's off-diagonal main obstruction at total length XM^2 > T is the bilinear form sum_{u != v} c(u)c(v)*kernel(log u/v) where the long variable carries Lambda-coefficients pinned by the explicit formula (the map localizes this exactly: O1_bound -> prop_PP -> tr2; 'beyond lambda = 1 the off-diagonal requires Hardy-Littlewood prime-pair information, equivalently Montgomery's PCC for alpha > 1'). The dangerous configurations are n, n' ~ T^lambda prime powers with m, m' <= M^2 and n*m ~ n'*m' (archimedean proximity |log(nm/n'm')| <~ 1/L — a size relation, not a congruence), i.e. Lambda-Lambda correlations along dilated shifts, decorated by mu-weights. By contrast, the twisted-second-moment literature the proposal invokes (BCHB 1985; Conrey's T^{4/7}; Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill T^{17/33}) evaluates integral |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 * |psi(t)|^2, where the length-T factor contributes DIVISOR coefficients d(n) via the approximate functional equation — smooth, factorable coefficients amenable to Kloosterman/spectral technology. Nothing in the mollifier twist converts the explicit formula's Lambda into d: the mu-average over m, m' does not supply the smooth long variable that dispersion/D-I methods require (Lambda is supported on primes; for each fixed (m, m') the sum is a genuine prime-pair correlation sum_n Lambda(n)Lambda((nm-h)/m'), and the (m,m')-average is over the SHORT variables only). So M3's 'proven multiplicative input strictly beyond bandwidth-one pair-correlation data' does not exist as claimed: at lambda = 1, theta > 0 the evaluation is HL-hard, exactly the wall the paper's Prop 5.6 hook names as requiring prime-pair asymptotics. The proposal's failure-mode list even senses trouble here but misdiagnoses it as a 'uniformity' risk rather than a coefficient-type mismatch. Note this finding is independent of Findings 1-2: even if the twisted moments WERE evaluable, their VALUES (Finding 1) give a vacuous certificate; and even if the values were favorable, the evaluation technology cited does not apply.

findings.claim: The DH/Epstein separation theorem (M4) is real but not new leverage: 'no antecedent' and 'the first positivity statement in this program whose engine requires the Euler product' are contradicted by the program's own record, and input-level separation is necessary-not-sufficient for RH-sensitivity in any case.
findings.argument: The campaign map states verbatim (map-hooks, transcript section): 'Davenport-Heilbronn-type functions (no Euler product): Sigma|c(n)|^2 grows like x^{1+delta}, Prop 5.6 fails, certificate empty — the correct RH-false control behavior.' So the UNMOLLIFIED engine already fails for DH at the level of inputs (polynomial boundedness of the log-derivative coefficients feeding Montgomery-Vaughan), with no mollifier involved; the proposal even concedes 'the paper already notes Prop 5.6 dies' and then claims the separation 'has no antecedent'. The mollified route adds a second, redundant failure mode (no bounded-coefficient Dirichlet inverse: 1/f has abscissa >= sigma_0 > 1 — a correct, standard abscissa lemma). Formalizing the pair as a theorem is honest instrument-building of modest value, but it does not convert proportion certificates into RH-sensitive statements: DH-separation at input level is compatible with the certificate family being capped at 0.68 and blind to o(N) off-line zeros (the proposal is honest about the o(N)-blindness, so this is a novelty-inflation finding, not a scope violation).

findings.claim: The AH/bandwidth-ceiling evasion is technically correct in the narrow formal sense but carries less content than claimed: in Regime I the mollified moments consume exactly the same unconditional arithmetic inputs (PNT-level Lambda-averages and MV bounds for total Dirichlet-polynomial length <= T) rearranged, and the two-level weighted statistics have per-variable Fourier support (lambda + theta) < 1.
findings.argument: The evasion argument says m1, m2 are 'twisted data outside the bandwidth-one class' on which the AH degeneracy and the 256-law are silent. Formally true: the 256-law ceiling covers linear pairings with the difference-type form factor, and the weighted statistics sum_rho w(gamma_rho) and sum w(gamma)w(gamma')K(gamma-gamma') with w = |B(1/2+i*gamma)|^2 are not functionals of the pair-correlation measure alone. But in Regime I (lambda + 2theta <= 1) every ingredient is evaluated from Lambda(n), n <= T^{lambda+2theta} <= T, via MV — the identical unconditional input window as the unmollified paper; the 'new' data class is a repackaging, and its own LP ceiling (which M6 promises to compute) has no reason to sit above 0.6818. Given Findings 1-2, the question is moot — the achievable sup of the new family is the OLD value + O(1/log T) — but the framing 'twisted arithmetic data provably invisible to bandwidth-one L2 data' overstates what Regime I actually reads: it is bandwidth-<=1 data read against a T-dependent oscillating weight, whose entire unconditional evaluation is PNT + MV.

findings.claim: Both proposed experiments have design flaws that would mask or confound the advertised go/no-go signals (though Experiment A would, ironically, immediately falsify the proposal's own m2 claim).
findings.argument: Experiment A: at T ~ 5000-9878 (l ~ 6.7-7.4), the proposed mollifier lengths M in {20, 100, 500, 2000} correspond to theta = log M / l up to ~1.1 — far outside every admissible regime (Regime I needs lambda + 2*theta <= 1, i.e. theta <= 0.16 at lambda = 0.68, i.e. M <= 3). The measured 'gain curve' at these parameters probes nothing about the asymptotic theorem; what it WILL show (per Finding 1's computed ratios, already 2.1-3.2 at M = 100-3000) is an inflation-dominated LOSS growing with log M — useful as a refutation of the proposal, useless as the calibration of a first-variation function G that does not exist in the claimed form. Experiment B (margin program) has an unaddressed support confounder: W_B(f, f) = W(b conv f, b conv f), and supp(b conv f) extends supp(f) by log M, so the mollified form on supports [1/X, X] is the RESTRICTION of the plain Weil form to a subspace of tests with support ~ X*M. The empirical margin law e^{-4piX} is pinned to the support endpoint (prolate leakage), so the natural prediction for the mollified margin is the LARGER-support floor e^{-4pi*X*M}-type — any measured slope change is contaminated by pure support bookkeeping unless the comparison is made at matched TOTAL support, which the protocol does not specify. The M5 'margin law with c < 4pi' conjecture is untested either way, but the experiment as designed cannot decide it.

verdicts.repairs: The affirmative program (M1's certificate as stated, M2's 'improved constant' branch, M3's targets of beating 0.6725/0.68183) is not salvageable — Findings 1-2 show the two-moment Gram functional has no favorable mollifier direction, with maximal net gain O(1/log T) over all real Dirichlet-polynomial weights. What IS salvageable, and worth doing: (1) Convert the route into its own pre-announced no-go outcome, but as a THEOREM rather than a contingency: prove 'mollification cannot help two-moment Weil-Gram certificates' — an explicit variance-cost/trace-gain trade-off (trace gain O(theta) vs Plancherel variance cost >= c*theta*l per unit amplitude-squared, hence sup over b of 2m1^2/m2 - 1 = unmollified + O(1/log T)). This is provable with exactly the Regime-I toolkit the proposal assembles (MV, Landau-Gonek, the corrected fourth-moment computation), is formalizable against the existing LP-ceiling/Stability templates, and adds a genuinely new entry to the no-go library: 'the first-substantive-step-is-an-evaluation' route dies by Jensen, not by Weil positivity — the mollifier has nothing to mollify because the explicit-formula atoms carry flat mass with no zeta'(rho) factor. (2) The 20-line weighted 2x2-block signature lemma and the configuration-free weighted rank-trace certificate (Lean hook section) are sound pure linear algebra and can be merged into RHLinalg regardless — they are weight-agnostic instruments, useful if anyone ever finds a weight family whose fourth moment is controlled (e.g. weights paired with a derivative factor, CGG-style, IF a Weil-form analogue carrying zeta'(rho) mass could be constructed — the one structural question this refutation leaves open and the only direction meriting a redesigned proposal). (3) Experiment A, re-aimed: run it to MEASURE the inflation ratio and the certificate loss versus the (log M)^2 law, closing the empirical case; drop the G(alpha) fit. (4) M4's separation lemmas can be kept as a small formalization exercise with honest framing ('formalizing a known input-level separation'), and Experiment B only after fixing the matched-total-support protocol.
literature_flags: The proposal's load-bearing claim '<|B|^4>/<|B|^2>^2 stays O(1) for the mu-mollifier' contradicts the standard fourth-moment computation for Mobius-coefficient Dirichlet polynomials (integral |sum_{m<=M} mu(m)m^{-1/2-it}|^4 dt ~ T(log M)^4, since sum (mu*mu)^2(n)/n has Dirichlet series zeta(s)^4*H(s)); verified numerically during this review (ratio 2.15 -> 3.21 monotone over M = 100 -> 3000 vs bounded ~1.6-1.9 for random signs). Any referee should check this one line first.

'Twisted second moment known to mollifier length T^{17/33}' (attributed to Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill): recalled as correct for integral |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 |psi(t)|^2 with divisor-type long variable, but needs verification of the exact exponent AND of the crucial scope point that this technology handles d(n)-coefficients from the approximate functional equation, not the Lambda(n)-coefficient bilinear forms the Gram form actually produces (Finding 3).

'Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek 1998 / Bui-Heath-Brown 2013 reach 19/27 simple under RH' — citation essentially right (CGG originally under RH+GLH; BHB removed GLH), but the proposal's analogy 'CGG made unconditional' silently swaps CGG's flat weight |B(rho)zeta'(rho)|^2 for the wild weight |B(rho)|^2 alone; the discrete mollified moments literature should be checked for the behavior of sum_rho |B(rho)|^{2,4} WITHOUT the zeta' factor (expected: divergent normalized fourth moment, matching Finding 1).

Gonek's uniform version of Landau's formula for x up to T^theta (error terms uniform in x): flagged by the proposal itself; the m1 evaluation survives at the heuristic level for theta < 2/3 but the uniformity constant should be checked before any writeup.

Davenport-Heilbronn zeros in sigma > 1 and the abscissa lemmas for -f'/f and 1/f (coefficients Omega(n^{sigma_0-1-eps})): standard and almost certainly fine, but note the program's own record (map-hooks transcript section) already contains the DH input-level failure of the unmollified method — the proposal's 'no antecedent' novelty claim should be checked against the Zeta23 paper's Section 1.5/Prop 5.6 remarks.

findings.claim: Tier 2 / M5 (unconditional 11/12, de-conditionalizing Ozluk) rests on a false tractability claim: the required arithmetic input — unconditional evaluation of the q-averaged form factor on (1,2), 'evaluable UNCONDITIONALLY by dispersion/asymptotic-large-sieve technology (Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan) for X up to Q^{2-eps}' — is the open variance-of-primes-in-arithmetic-progressions problem in disguise, out of reach of the cited technology at EVERY fixed Lambda > 1, including the proposal's own fallback Lambda = 1 + c.
findings.argument: Reduction: averaging the second moment over q ~ Q and all chi mod q converts the off-diagonal chi(n)chibar(m) terms into sum_{q~Q} w(q/Q) sum_{n≡m (q), n,m<=X} Lambda(n)Lambda(m) = sum_{n,m<=X} Lambda(n)Lambda(m) #{q~Q : q | n-m} — precisely the Barban-Davenport-Halberstam/Montgomery-Hooley variance sum_{q~Q} sum_a (psi(X;q,a) - X/phi(q))^2 reorganized. The form-factor plateau F_fam = 1+o(1) on (1, Lambda) at X = Q^Lambda is EQUIVALENT to the variance asymptotic (main term Qx log Q + c Qx with error o(Qx log Q)) at Q = X^{1/Lambda}. Unconditionally, Montgomery-Hooley carries an irreducible error term O(x^2 (log x)^{-A}) of Siegel-Walfisz origin; the main term is Qx log x ~ x^{1+1/Lambda} log x, so the asymptotic is known ONLY for Q >= x/(log x)^A, i.e. effective bandwidth Lambda <= 1 + O(A loglog x / log x) -> 1 — worth exactly nothing in the limiting constant (kappa stays 4/3, certificate stays 2/3). For ANY fixed Lambda > 1 (moduli Q = x^{1/Lambda}, x^{1/2} < Q < x^{1-delta}) the variance asymptotic is a notorious open problem; under GRH it holds — which is EXACTLY where Ozluk's GRH is load-bearing. Even an upper bound of the right constant fails: the classical large sieve gives (X + Q^2)||a||^2 against a diagonal main term ~ (sum_{q~Q} phi(q))||a||^2 ≈ 0.30·Q^2||a||^2, a lossy factor ~3.3 that makes the certificate 2 - kappa negative; closing that gap asymptotically for Lambda(n)-coefficients IS the open problem. The asymptotic large sieve of CIS does not do it: its asymptotic evaluations exploit divisor-type coefficients (d_3, Voronoi/factorization structure) and for Lambda-coefficients its 'main terms' are precisely the unevaluated averaged shifted convolutions sum_d sum_j Lambda(n)Lambda(n+jd) — it reorganizes the problem, it does not solve it (parity). Barrier-zoo instantiation: in a world with an exceptional character psi mod r (Siegel zero beta_0), Lambda(n) carries a bias ~ -psi(n)n^{beta_0-1}, and the variance/plateau on (1,2) acquires anomalous secondary terms (Friedlander-Granville irregularities; Fiorilli's analysis of exceptional-zero influence on BDH ranges Q = x^theta); that world satisfies every input Tier 2 legitimately consumes (orthogonality, per-character explicit formula, RvM, the T0 taper, dispersion identities), so no proof from those inputs alone can establish the plateau — establishing it unconditionally requires excluding/controlling exceptional characters, i.e. a breakthrough, not 'months 18-30 engineering'. Consequences: (a) the thesis sentence '...yielding unconditional two-thirds (and, with q-averaging, eleven-twelfths) theorems ... once one classical missing lemma (a Gevrey/Ingham-class taper) is supplied' is FALSE as stated — 11/12 needs a second, open, hard input that the taper does not supply; (b) the fallback in failure-mode 3 ('stall at Lambda = 1+c', 'averaged 0.70-0.75, still past the bandwidth-one ceiling') is ALSO open for every fixed c > 0 (e.g. 0.725 needs Lambda ≈ 1.1, i.e. moduli Q = x^{0.91}, outside the Montgomery-Hooley polylog window), so no beyond-ceiling family certificate follows from known technology at all; (c) 'unconditional refutation of AH on average' as a by-product inherits the same status; (d) the claimed de-conditionalization analogy ('GRH removed by the rank-trace mechanism, the same de-conditionalization the paper performed on Montgomery') mislocates where GRH enters Ozluk: the anchor paper removed RH used as a ZERO-LOCATION hypothesis, with the arithmetic side (MV, |alpha|<1 complex form factor, BGSTB) already unconditional; in Ozluk's (1,2) range GRH is load-bearing on the ARITHMETIC side (primes in APs to large moduli), which the arithmetic-free zero side + rank-trace cannot touch by construction (the Lean map states it: 'new arithmetic must enter through the PaperInputs boundary'). M5's headline payoffs ('highest unconditional proportion in any family', 'GRH removed from Ozluk', 'AH refuted on family average', 'first certificate consuming beyond-bandwidth-one data') should all be re-labeled conditional on an unproven arithmetic hypothesis.

findings.claim: Several 'first'/novelty claims are exposed to prior art in the family-statistics literature, in particular unconditional extended-support results for the q-aggregated Dirichlet family (Drappeau-Pratt-Radziwill one-level density with support beyond 2, via BFI/Deshouillers-Iwaniec, no GRH), which already demonstrate 'beyond-bandwidth-one family data' for linear statistics.
findings.argument: The proposal claims (Payoff, M5) 'Partial M5 (Lambda = 1+c) already demonstrates a certificate consuming beyond-bandwidth-one data, the first of its kind', and (Novelty 2) 'No proportion-of-zeros-on-the-line theorem at height polylogarithmic in the conductor exists in any family'. Two exposures: (a) Drappeau-Pratt-Radziwill, 'One-level density estimates for Dirichlet L-functions with extended support' proved, unconditionally, one-level density for the q-averaged Dirichlet family with test support strictly beyond [-2,2] (i.e. beyond the orthogonality-diagonal range, using primes in APs to moduli > x^{1/2} on average via well-factorable/Kloosterman technology). This is LINEAR-statistic data, not the bilinear second moment the certificate needs — so it does not rescue Tier 2 (finding 1) — but it does mean the currency 'unconditional family form-factor-type data beyond the conductor bandwidth' already exists in the literature, weakening the 'first of its kind' rhetoric and requiring precise scoping (linear vs bilinear) in any published novelty claim. (b) The low-height (T = polylog q) regime overlaps a literature on zeros of Dirichlet L-functions near the central point / low-lying zeros (Iwaniec-Sarnak nonvanishing, Hughes-Rudnick n-level densities at fixed q with support up to 2, Fiorilli-Martin) that must be checked before asserting no polylog-height proportion theorem exists; the proposal flags CIS/Wu constants but not this adjacent body. Not fatal — F1's specific shape (proportion of ALL zeros in (T,2T] at T = (log q)^{1+delta}, simple-and-on-line, 2/3 constant) does appear genuinely absent from the literature — but the novelty section needs the audit it promises.

findings.claim: Mechanism-level nits in Tier 1 that survive audit but need honest bookkeeping: the dual-term bound 'L^2 X/q' is stated without divisor/kernel-weight losses; the chi0-removal and edge-of-range arithmetic at Lambda = 1 - 1/loglog q is borderline against the constraint T <= q^{1/loglog q}; and novelty claim (7) ('t-aspect certificate provably invisible at all computable heights') sits on an internal contradiction in the program's own map.
findings.argument: (a) Dual terms: pairs nm ≡ 1 mod q, n,m <= X. Writing nm = 1 + jq, j <= X^2/q, the sum sum Lambda(n)Lambda(m)/sqrt(nm) over factorizations carries divisor-function multiplicity and the per-pair grid-kernel weight (O(L^2) in the MV currency); the honest bound is L^2 (X/q) · polylog, not L^2 X/q. Harmless — X/q <= e^{-log q/loglog q} T annihilates any polylog — but the stated bound is sloppy and a referee will make them redo it. (b) At Lambda = 1 - 1/loglog q with T <= q^{1/loglog q}, X = (qT)^Lambda < q holds only with the right constant in the exponent (log X = Lambda(log q + log T) <= (1 - 1/loglog q)(1 + 1/loglog q)log q = (1 - O(1/loglog^2 q))log q); the margin is real but thin, consistent with (and the source of) the C/loglog q losses — fine, but the F1 statement's A(delta) <= 2 + 2delta bookkeeping must be checked against exactly this chain. (c) The map's read:paper-method section says the flat-window certificate is '≈ +0.40 to +0.42' at accessible heights while lean:certificate says 'strictly negative at all computationally accessible heights (Remark 5.9, §8)'; the proposal's novelty claim (7) and Part-B selling point ('positive averaged certificate at q=997 is itself a first') depend on the second reading. Resolve against the actual paper §8 before publishing the claim. (d) Conversely, failure-mode 1's fear that the Ingham crossover radius r0 grows with L is unfounded: the convolving measure psi (widths w_j, sum w_j = w/2, w = 1) is L-independent, and the only L-dependent factor 2sin((L-w)r/2)/r is uniformly bounded by 2/|r| — the decay onset is a constant depending on delta only. The taper lemma T0 itself checks out: it is the classical Ingham construction (product of sincs with widths c_delta·w/(j(log(j+2))^{1+delta}); prod_{j<=J(r)} 1/(w_j r) = exp(-c|r|/(log|r|)^{1+delta}) with J(r) ≍ w|r|/(log|r|)^{1+delta}; strip factor e^{|y|L/2} from |sin z| <= e^{|Im z|} across total support), Ingham's integral criterion is correctly invoked, and the tail arithmetic T/(log T)^{1+delta} >> log q loglog q ⟸ T >= (log q)^{1+delta'} with D0 = T/loglog q is right.

findings.claim: M4 (GL(2) families) is plausible but its bandwidth claim depends on which average is running: plain Petersson at fixed weight and fixed level gives only nm <= conductor^{1-eps}, i.e. Lambda* = 1/2 — vacuous by the dimension cap; the claimed Lambda* = 1 needs the k-average (i^{-k} oscillation) in the weight aspect or c ≡ 0 mod N in the prime-level aspect, plus unbudgeted harmonic-weight removal and orthogonal-symmetry corrections.
findings.argument: Petersson: sum_f w_f lambda_f(n)lambda_f(m) = delta_{n=m} + 2πi^{-k} sum_c S(n,m;c)/c · J_{k-1}(4π√(nm)/c). At fixed weight k, level 1, the Bessel term is only negligible for √(nm) << k, i.e. nm <= conductor^{1-eps} (conductor ~ k^2); with both n,m <= X this forces X <= cond^{1/2-eps}, Lambda* = 1/2, where the formalized dimension cap makes the certificate empty (the proposal's own evasion section stresses this threshold). The proposal's chosen regimes do fix this — weight-averaged k <= K (the ILS trick: the i^{-k} sum over k kills Kloosterman terms up to √(nm) <= K^{2-eps}, so nm <= cond^{2-eps}, Lambda* -> 1) and prime level N with fixed weight (c ≡ 0 mod N forces the Bessel argument <= 4π√(nm)/N, negligible for nm <= N^{2-eps}) — so the design is sound, but the text's one-line justification ('Kloosterman off-diagonal killed by Bessel decay for n,m <= conductor^{1-eps}') states the WRONG range (it is nm, not each of n,m, and the quadratic extension is average-specific, not plain Bessel decay). Additional unpriced items: (i) harmonic weights w_f ~ 1/||f||^2 must be removed to convert weighted zero proportions to natural ones (standard but constant-consuming); (ii) the family is orthogonal/symplectic-symmetry-typed, so the averaged prime side carries lambda_f(p^2) = lambda_f(p)^2 - 1 symmetric-square terms whose family average contributes a non-unitary correction to the two-point input; at window height T = polylog(cond) this should be lower order, but nothing in the proposal budgets it. The proposal's own failure mode ('M4 constant could land below 2/3') is the honest reading; the milestone survives at reduced confidence.

verdicts.repairs: 1) TIER 1 STANDS — keep it as the program. The core mechanism audit passes: certificate additivity over block-diagonal direct sums is genuine linear algebra; for X < q character orthogonality kills the off-diagonal AND the mu-P cross terms identically (both are linear in chi(n), and n <= X < q forces n = 1); the chi0-removal (d·sup|P| ~ L·T·√X per family, o(phi(q)T l_q)) and dual-term (nm ≡ 1 mod q) bounds go through with the noted polylog corrections; the averaged kappa reproduces 1/Lambda + Lambda/3 (verified via the alpha-integral: [Lambda + 2∫_0^Lambda(Lambda-a)a da]/Lambda^2); kappa_fam(2) = 13/12 and 2 - 13/12 = 11/12 exactly match Ozluk, confirming the Tier-2 bookkeeping is internally consistent; the T0 taper is the correct classical Ingham construction and the T >= (log q)^{1+delta} arithmetic closes; the numerics parameters (L, X, d at q = 100003/997) all check. F1 is credibly provable in the stated window and would be judged on its honest 'on average over chi' scope with the Markov corollaries. 2) FIX THE THESIS AND M5: decouple 11/12 from 'once one classical missing lemma is supplied'. State M5 as conditional on a named open hypothesis — 'unconditional q-averaged variance asymptotic for Lambda in progressions at Q = x^{1/Lambda}, Lambda in (1,2)' (equivalently the family form-factor plateau) — and record that this hypothesis is (a) exactly where Ozluk's GRH sits, (b) beyond Montgomery-Hooley (whose unconditional range Q >= x/(log x)^A gives only Lambda = 1 + O(loglog/log), worth nothing in the constant), (c) not delivered by the CIS asymptotic large sieve for Lambda-coefficients (parity/divisor-structure), and (d) entangled with exceptional characters (Fiorilli/Friedlander-Granville), so its unconditional proof is Siegel-adjacent. Replace the false fallback claim ('Lambda = 1+c still beats the ceiling') with the honest one: known technology yields nothing past bandwidth 1 + o(1) in this family; a genuinely available intermediate deliverable is the Montgomery-Hooley-regime certificate at Lambda = 1 + O(A loglog q/log q) — a conceptual 'certificate consuming a vanishing sliver of beyond-bandwidth-one data' with no constant gain, publishable only as a proof-of-mechanism. 3) Re-scope the AH by-product as conditional on the same hypothesis. 4) M4: rewrite the bandwidth justification (nm <= cond^{2-eps} via k-average resp. c ≡ 0 mod N, not plain Bessel decay), and budget harmonic-weight removal and the symmetric-square correction explicitly. 5) Before publication, run the promised literature audit with these additions: Drappeau-Pratt-Radziwill extended-support one-level density (prior art for beyond-bandwidth-one family arithmetic, linear statistics), Hughes-Rudnick/Fiorilli-Martin low-height family statistics (novelty claim 2), Harper-Soundararajan variance lower bounds (calibrates hardness of the Tier-2 input), and resolve the internal contradiction about the sign of the t-aspect certificate at accessible heights before selling Part B's 'positive at q = 997' as a first. With repairs 2-3, the direction is an honest, strong instrument-building program whose deliverables F1 + M3 + M6 + taper are real and whose horizon is correctly priced.
literature_flags: Ozluk (J. Number Theory 1996, and 1982 thesis): verify exact statement — GRH-conditional q-averaged form factor F_Q(alpha) for |alpha| < 2 and the 11/12 simple-zeros constant, and WHERE GRH enters (arithmetic side: primes in APs error terms). The proposal's de-conditionalization analogy depends on this being zero-side only, which is almost certainly false.

Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan 'asymptotic large sieve': verify that its asymptotic evaluations require divisor-type/smooth coefficients (d_3, Voronoi structure) and do NOT evaluate Lambda-coefficient bilinear forms for N in (Q, Q^{2-eps}); also verify their aggregate-family critical-zeros proportion (proposal recalls ~56-58%).

Montgomery-Hooley asymptotic and refinements (Goldston-Vaughan): confirm the unconditional range Q >= x/(log x)^A and the Siegel-Walfisz origin of the x^2(log x)^{-A} error; this is the load-bearing fact behind finding 1.

Fiorilli (and Friedlander-Granville): exceptional-zero influence on the BDH/variance asymptotic in ranges Q = x^theta, theta < 1 — cited from memory as the Siegel-entanglement argument; verify the precise statements.

Drappeau-Pratt-Radziwill, 'One-level density estimates for Dirichlet L-functions with extended support' (~2020): unconditional, q-averaged, support beyond [-2,2] — prior art against 'first beyond-bandwidth-one family data' rhetoric; verify support value and unconditionality.

Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh arXiv:2306.04799: confirms the anchor paper's de-conditionalization pattern was zero-side (complex-zero form factor |alpha| < 1 unconditional) — supports the disanalogy in finding 1.

Wu 2019 (~41.7% per character, log q = o(log T)) and any Levinson-type results for Dirichlet L at small T (Bauer; low-height literature): needed for novelty claim (2) 'no polylog-height proportion theorem in any family'.

Conrey 1983 (xi^(k) zeros: on-line proportion -> 1 unconditionally, strip containment of xi^(k) zeros) and Farmer-Gonek-Lee (RH-conditional simplicity constants): both recalled from memory and load-bearing for sub-direction (ii)'s honesty framing.
Harper-Soundararajan (unconditional LOWER bounds for variance of primes in APs): calibrates that only lower bounds, not asymptotics, are known at Q = x^theta, theta < 1 — corroborates finding 1.
Hughes-Rudnick (fixed-q n-level densities, support < 2) and Iwaniec-Sarnak nonvanishing: check for hidden polylog-height proportion-type statements adjacent to F1.

findings.claim: The load-bearing claim that ⟨|B|⁴⟩/⟨|B|²⟩² = O(1) for the Möbius mollifier is false — it diverges like (log M)² — so First Theorem part (ii) is false as stated for the headline weight family, and the advertised order-θ certificate gain does not exist at full mollifier amplitude.
findings.argument: For b_m = μ(m)ψ(log(M/m)/log M), the fourth moment ⟨|B(1/2+iτ)|⁴⟩ over τ ∈ [T,2T] is, by Montgomery–Vaughan (valid since M² ≤ T in Regime I), Σ_{n≤M²} |Σ_{mm'=n} b_m b_{m'}|²/n. For squarefree n with ω(n)=k the inner sum is (−1)^k Σ_{S⊆factors} ψψ — all 2^k terms have the SAME sign (ψ ≥ 0), so no cancellation: |c_n| ≍ 2^{ω(n)}·(profile averages). Hence the sum is ≍ Σ μ²(n)4^{ω(n)}/n ≍ (log M)⁴ (Euler product ∏(1+4/p) ~ ζ⁴; smoothing with ψ(0)=0 changes constants, not log-powers, since the growth is bulk-multiplicative, not an edge effect). Since ⟨|B|²⟩ = Σ b_m²/m ≍ log M, the ratio is ≍ (log M)² = (θ log T)² → ∞. This quantity genuinely enters m2's diagonal term: the Frobenius kernel Φ(τ−τ')² has width ~1/L = 1/(λ log T), smaller than B's variation scale 1/log M (θ < λ), so ν_B(τ)ν_B(τ') ≈ |B(τ)|⁴·(smooth)² on the kernel support — the diagonal term is the mollifier fourth moment, not ⟨|B|²⟩². Consequence: for M = T^θ with fixed θ > 0, ‖G^B‖²_F/N ~ c·(θ log T)²·(1/λ) diverges, so the constant m2(b,λ) asserted in Theorem part (ii) does not exist for the theorem's own headline family (b depends on T through M = T^θ), and the certificate 2m1²/m2 − 1 → −1: vacuous. The claimed gain m1 = 1 + 2θÃ is correct (I verified the sign: the μ-weight resonates with zeros since 1/ζ is large at zeros, via Landau–Gonek Σ_ρ|B(ρ)|² = N·n(b) − (T/π)𝒞(b) with 𝒞 < 0), but it is bought at a (log M)²-divergent Frobenius cost because the Gram certificate is QUARTIC in B where CGG's discrete-moment method is only quadratic — the structural difference the proposal's 'CGG made unconditional' framing obscures. The proposal's own failure-mode list item 2 (log-normal fluctuation of β_ρ inflating m2) names this risk, but the mechanism section asserts its negation, and the mechanism is what the milestone payoffs are computed from. Repairable (see repairs), but the repair demotes the gain from O(θ) to O(θ²).

findings.claim: In Regime I (λ + 2θ ≤ 1) mollification is asymptotically dominated by simply widening the window, so M1/M2 will almost certainly produce the pre-registered no-go rather than an improved constant; all real value concentrates in Regime II (M3), which requires genuinely new unconditional 'weighted pair correlation' technology.
findings.argument: Total prime support of the mollified test k = (b⋆f_k)∗(b⋆f_l)~ is L + 2log M, i.e. effective bandwidth λ_tot = λ + 2θ. Compare spending the budget on the window: the unmollified CS certificate at λ_tot gains dV = 2θ·2|κ'(λ)|/κ² = O(θ) (κ' = −1/λ²+1/3 < 0 for λ < √3). The mollified gain, after the repair forced by finding 1, is bounded as follows: any weight direction c has trace gain (per Landau–Gonek normalization, one 1/log T per Λ-insertion) ≤ (1/L')Σ_p (log p/p)|c_p| ≤ √(n(c))·θ·O(1) by Cauchy–Schwarz against Σ_{p≤M}(log p)²/p = (log M)²/2, while the quartic Frobenius penalty is ≥ (2/λ)n(c)·(1+o(1)) (the ε²-term of ⟨|B|⁴⟩/n(b)²: 4⟨(ReC)²⟩+2⟨|C|²⟩−2n(c) = 2n(c)). Optimizing amplitude (max_x aθx − bx², attained by the log-weighted prime resonator c_p ∝ log p) gives net gain a²θ²/4b = O(θ²) — strictly smaller than the O(θ) window gain for all admissible θ. So within λ+2θ ≤ 1 the mollification-vs-bandwidth exchange rate is provably unfavorable at the level of main terms, and M2's outcome is predictable in advance: the no-go branch. The route's genuine content is therefore Regime II (λ = 1, θ > 0, total support 1+2θ > 1), where the window CANNOT be widened (MV wall) but the mollifier CAN add support because the off-diagonals become Λ×(b⋆b̄) shifted-convolution sums — Λ-versus-divisor-type correlations, which ARE evaluable by dispersion/Deshouillers–Iwaniec/BCR technology where pure Λ×Λ (Hardy–Littlewood) is not. That IS a real, DH-violating, beyond-bandwidth-one input, and it is the honest core of the proposal — but it is unproven new analysis (adapting Kloosterman-technology twisted second moments to the Φ-smoothed Gabor bilinear form with |B|⁴-weights of length T^{4θ}), and the achievable gain feeding through it is O(θ²) with θ realistically ≤ 17/132-ish if the |B|⁴-length constraint 4θ ≤ 17/33 binds.

findings.claim: The milestone payoffs are miscomputed and the dependency order is broken: the first theorem's CS-branch baseline (1/2, distinct) is strictly below the paper's existing constants, and M3's headline targets (beat 0.6725, then the 0.6818287 ceiling — both SIMPLE-zero functionals) require the weighted-atom saturation control that is deferred to M5 and flagged there as possibly unreachable.
findings.argument: The first theorem certifies N₀^dist ≥ (2m1²/m2 − 1)N, unmollified value 1/2 at λ=1 — below the paper's existing distinct-zero constant (5/6 via Theorem C's k_c=3 pricing) and below its simple-zero 2/3. The proposal's own Lemma-R branch with weights gives only (m1²/m2)N = 3/4·N unmollified — still below 5/6, because continuous effective masses tβ_ρ forfeit the integrality pricing k_c(m) that produces 2/3 and 5/6; recovering it needs per-atom saturation control governed by the fourth mollified DISCRETE moment (distribution of β_ρ over zeros), which the proposal itself places in M5 and lists as 'potentially out of reach unconditionally'. Therefore: (a) M1 delivers no constant that beats any existing record — it is purely a machinery/instrument paper (which the payoff section half-admits); (b) M3's target 'V(1,θ*) > 0.6725' compares against the Montgomery–Taylor SIMPLE-zero optimum, but the only mollified branches available before M5 certify distinct-type counts from a 1/2–3/4 baseline; the required gain (+0.086 in m1²/m2 just to reach 0.836 on the CS branch) is far beyond the O(θ²) resonator gain at any admissible θ; (c) the stretch claim 'first certificate strictly beyond the formalized bandwidth-one ceiling' conflates functionals — the 0.6818287 ceiling is for the simple-zero proportion (the map notes explicitly that the 256-law does not cover the distinct-zeros functional, which would need separate LPs), so beating it requires the simple branch, i.e. M5's machinery, inverting the stated M3→M5 order. The true dependency chain is: G-sign computation → M1 (repaired) → M5's bounded-variance saturation control → M3's twisted technology → any headline constant. Three stacked uncertainties (G > 0; saturation control; Regime-II uniformity), each individually plausible, jointly maybe 10–15%.

findings.claim: Experiment A's parameter grid is far outside every admissible regime of the theorem it is meant to validate, so its 'closure check' cannot test the moment identities' error budget.
findings.argument: At the proposed height (first 10⁴ zeros, γ ≤ 9878), log(T/2π) ≈ 7.3, so M = 2000 corresponds to θ = log M/log(T/2π) ≈ 1.04 and even M = 100 gives θ ≈ 0.63 — while the theorem requires λ + 2θ ≤ 1 with λ = 1 forcing θ = 0. At these parameters the total Dirichlet-polynomial length XM² is ~T³, where the MV off-diagonal bound (the entire unconditionality mechanism) fails by orders of magnitude, so 2–3-digit agreement between zero-side sums and the derived prime-side main terms would neither confirm nor disconfirm the theorem's bookkeeping — at best it probes the finite-size analogue of the identities, dominated by uncontrolled off-diagonal terms. The DIFFERENCE-measurement design (mollified minus unmollified at matched windows) is sound and the paper's +0.40–0.42 finite-T baseline is quoted correctly, but the go/no-go G-sign datum should be extracted at θ ≤ 0.1–0.2 equivalent (M ≤ 5), or at 10⁵–10⁶ zeros from Odlyzko tables, for the sign to bear on the asymptotic claim.

findings.claim: The 'CGG made unconditional' novelty framing overstates mechanism continuity with Conrey–Ghosh–Gonek; the actual mechanism is a resonance/amplification argument, not CGG's damping argument, and cannot recover 19/27 even conditionally.
findings.argument: CGG (1998; RH-sufficiency by Bui–Heath-Brown 2013) bound simple zeros via (Σ_ρ M(ρ)ζ'(ρ))²/Σ_ρ|M(ρ)ζ'(ρ)|² — the mollifier appears LINEARLY in the numerator and QUADRATICALLY per zero in the denominator, and works by damping (Mζ' ≈ (ζ'/ζ)-truncation has controlled second moment). The Gram certificate here has |B|² per zero in the trace and |B|⁴ in the Frobenius norm — the weight amplifies the count via zero-prime resonance (Landau–Gonek) rather than damping a ζ'-weight, which is exactly why the quartic penalty of finding 1 arises with no CGG analogue. The honest genealogy is Soundararajan-style resonance + the Zeta23 inertia frame, a new combination (the frame is one day old, so trivially unclaimed) — genuinely novel, not a resurfaced refuted idea, but an expert's afternoon check on |B|⁴ would produce finding 1; the closest genuinely-adjacent prior art (conditional weighted statistics: Fazzari's weighted one-level densities, |ζ'(ρ)|-weighted pair correlations) is correctly flagged by the proposal as RH-conditional.

findings.claim: M4's separation theorem is true and cheap but its content is partly definitional, and it should be re-ordered first in the milestone ladder.
findings.argument: The abscissa lemmas are correct: Davenport–Heilbronn (1936) and class-number > 1 Epstein zeta functions have zeros with σ₀ > 1 (classical; DH fine structure in Bombieri–Ghosh), so −f'/f and 1/f have Dirichlet-series abscissae ≥ σ₀ > 1, giving coefficient growth Ω(n^{σ₀−1−ε}) that destroys both the MV second-moment evaluation and any bounded-coefficient mollifier. But 'the certificate family is provably empty at the level of inputs' requires defining the family BY the requirement that the input asymptotics hold, then showing they fail — a theorem whose content is largely the definition, and which does not show that no certificate of a broader shape exists for these objects (nor need it, given the honest proportion-only scope). As a formalized multiplicativity-sensitive yes-go/no-go pair it has real methodological value for the program's refutation channel, is independent of M1–M3, and is the lowest-risk deliverable on the list — it should be first, both for morale and because it sharpens exactly which inputs the Regime-II analysis must consume.

findings.claim: The obstruction-evasion section is essentially sound — the best in this respect I have refereed against this canon — and the zero-side structural claims check out against the Lean artifact.
findings.argument: Verified point by point: (a) the bandwidth-one ceiling's formal scope caveat (full-map line 122) explicitly lists 'mollifiers/Levinson–Conrey machinery, amplification' as outside the certificate class, because m1(b), m2(b) are zero-prime correlation data that the 256-periodic pure-configuration law cannot reproduce — the escape is legitimate, not a loophole-lawyering move; (b) lemmaR_tight is tightness relative to the fixed invariant list, and supplying a new invariant pair reuses rank_trace_mult_k unchanged — the map confirms it is stated leak-free for arbitrary real weights m_j ≥ 0 (RankTraceMult.lean:369), so the proposed 20-line signature lemma for [[0,w],[w̄,0]] plus the weighted Prop 4.1-B is a realistic first formalizable statement; (c) the σ-equivariance argument is right: the weight enters as the scalar m_ρB(ρ)conj(B(1−ρ̄)) respecting ρ ↦ 1−ρ̄ (an off-line pair has 1−ρ̄ at the same ordinate γ, and the 2×2 block has signature (1,1) or (0,0)), so Lemma 3.1 pull-back inertia applies verbatim; (d) AH constrains only difference-variable form-factor data and is silent on Σ_ρ|B(ρ)|²-type one-level resonance sums; (e) the mollified first moment via Landau–Gonek is unconditional, with the uniformity-in-M caveat correctly self-flagged (rational x = mn/m' terms need Gonek's error terms with ⟨x⟩-denominators summed over pairs). The dimension cap, κ ≥ 2/√3, parity, Bombieri–Garrett, Conrey–Li, and Rodgers–Tao items are all handled honestly.

verdicts.repairs: 1) Restate the first theorem over bounded-variance weight families: require n_tail(b) = Σ_{m≥2} b_m²/m = O(1) uniformly in T (amplitude-damped resonators, e.g. c_p = −η log p/log M with η ≍ θ, rather than the full μψ-mollifier whose n_tail ≍ log M). In that class ⟨|B|⁴⟩/⟨|B|²⟩² = 1 + O(n_tail) genuinely is O(1), part (ii)'s constants m1(b,λ), m2(b,λ) exist, and the whole architecture goes through; the honest optimized gain is O(θ²) (max of aθx − bx² over amplitude x), not O(θ). Alternatively state (ii) with T-dependent m2 and record the (θ log T)² divergence as a theorem — it is itself the clean quantitative form of 'the Gram certificate is quartic in the mollifier', worth a remark. 2) Reorder milestones: M4 (separation lemmas, independent and cheap) first; then the G(α)-sign computation and corrected numerics (M ≤ 5 at 10⁴ zeros, or 10⁵–10⁶ zeros for θ ≈ 0.1–0.2) as an explicit gate BEFORE the full M1 proof; fold the bounded-variance saturation analysis (β_ρ concentrated near 1, where k_c integrality pricing survives with O(θ²) leakage — plausible precisely in the repaired regime) into M1/M2 rather than M5, since M3's targets depend on it. 3) Retarget M3 honestly: the deliverable is 'unconditional weighted pair correlation at effective support 1 + 2θ' — mean values of Λ×(b⋆b̄) shifted convolutions of total length T^{1+2θ} via dispersion/Deshouillers–Iwaniec/BCR — plugged into the map's named interface (one EvBound field with X > T in Prop 5.6's off-diagonal). That theorem is the prize independent of certificate arithmetic: it would be the first proven input strictly beyond bandwidth one, and the LP-template (M6) prices it before it is proven. State the constant targets against the correct functionals (distinct vs simple), computing the mollified k_c branch, and drop the 'beats 0.68183' stretch claim unless the simple-zero branch with saturation control is in hand. 4) Keep the margin program (M5b) but demote it to exploratory: its first instance (baby Euler weights on [1/3,3]) is cheap and its outcome redirects rather than gates. With these repairs the direction is a sound instrument-plus-priced-conjecture program; my probability for the repaired first theorem in 2 years by a strong group is 0.5–0.6 (designer's 0.6 is fair for the repaired statement, but the literal stated theorem is false in part (ii) for its headline family, for which my survival probability is ~0.2).
literature_flags: FALSE RECALLED CLAIM (my finding 1): 'mollifier fourth moments' giving ⟨|B|⁴⟩/⟨|B|²⟩² = O(1) for the length-T^θ Möbius mollifier — no such result exists; the standard 4^ω(n) computation gives ≍ (log M)². The O(1) statement is true only for bounded-variance (resonator-normalized) weights.

Gonek's uniform version of Landau's formula (Σ_{0<γ≤T} x^ρ, uniform in x; Gonek 1993 'An explicit formula of Landau and its applications'): the error terms for rational non-integer x = mn/m' (⟨x⟩-denominators summed over mollifier pairs) must be checked for M ≤ T^θ — the proposal flags this itself; it is load-bearing for m1.

Bettin–Chandee–Radziwiłł twisted second moment of ζ with Dirichlet-polynomial length T^{17/33}: verify attribution and exact exponent; also note the Regime-II object needs |B|⁴-weights (length T^{4θ}), so the binding constraint may be 4θ ≤ 17/33, not 2θ.

Conrey–Ghosh–Gonek 1998 (19/27 simple zeros): verify whether the original hypothesis is RH or GRH, and the precise role of Bui–Heath-Brown 2013 in reducing it to RH — cited correctly in spirit but the mechanism analogy is overstated (see finding 5).

Davenport–Heilbronn 1936 (II) / Bombieri–Ghosh: zeros with σ > 1 for the DH function and for Epstein zeta functions of class number > 1 — needed as the σ₀ > 1 input to M4's abscissa lemmas; classical but the precise statements should be pinned before formalizing.

Proposal's own flag, endorsed: 2025–26 'weighted pair correlation' literature (|ζ'(ρ)|²-weighted pair correlation; Fazzari's weighted one-level densities) — all instances known to me are RH-conditional with no unconditional on-line counts, but a literature pass is required before publishing the framing.

Unverified assertion: that Radziwiłł's mollifier limitations (arXiv:1207.6583) and the θ = 4/7 Conrey/Deshouillers–Iwaniec length barrier 'do not transfer to the Gram-moment functional' — plausible (different functional) but asserted without argument; the transfer question should be examined, since the same shifted-convolution inputs appear in Regime II.

findings.claim: T1's headline novelty ('first unconditional triple correlation for zeta, strictly stronger than anything in print') is overstated: it is a careful write-up of technology the parent artifact itself asserts as available, and its status as a 'first' hinges entirely on an unverified reading of Rudnick-Sarnak 1996.
findings.argument: Three independent deflations. (a) The Zeta23 paper itself asserts (Section 7.5(e), full-map.md line 92) that 'the diagonal method evaluates tr G-hat^k exactly in the Rudnick-Sarnak range k*lambda < 2' -- i.e., the artifact's authors regard the equal-window unconditional case as known technology, merely never written with error terms. A theorem the parent paper asserts in a remark is not 'strictly stronger than anything in print' in the sense the proposal's payoff section implies; it is the write-up of an assertion. (b) The artifact reads Hejhal 1994 / Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 as RH-conditional (full-map.md line 95: 'Under RH the third trace/triple correlation is a theorem [Hej94, RS96] for lambda<1'), which supports the proposal, BUT Rudnick-Sarnak's Duke 1996 paper is widely recalled to contain a remark that for zeta their n-level results hold unconditionally with complex ordinates (their test functions are Paley-Wiener, entire of exponential type -- exactly what complex-ordinate de-conditionalization needs). If that remark exists and is sound, T1 reduces to: explicit error terms + trace-formalism packaging of a 30-year-old theorem. The proposal flags this itself, but then still books M2 as 'standalone headline theorem (first unconditional triple correlation)' -- the milestone payoff is priced on the optimistic branch of an unresolved literature question. (c) The 'mixed windows' framing is novelty relative to the Zeta23 paper's tr G^k equal-window presentation, not relative to the literature: Rudnick-Sarnak's theorem is stated for general test functions with Fourier support in the simplex sum|xi_i| < 2, which already contains every kernel the mixed-window construction can produce. My own computation (finding 2) confirms the union of mixed-window boxes over sigma < 2 is exactly the open RS simplex -- i.e., mixed windows recover, via crude MV, precisely the data class RS already defined. Correct classification: T1 = new combination / careful de-conditionalized write-up (BGSTB24 precedent shows such write-ups are genuinely publishable and nontrivial -- BGSTB was new in 2023 despite RS's remark), not a new object. The BGSTB precedent is the strongest argument that T1 has real content; the proposal should be reframed around it.

findings.claim: The support bookkeeping conflates the window-sum sigma = lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c with the kernel's simplex support, and the flagship mixed-window example is numerically wrong: (0.98, 0.5, 0.5) does NOT put any factor at pair-bandwidth ~1; it reaches only |xi| <= 0.74.
findings.argument: Write the kernel Phi_a(g1-g2)Phi_b(g2-g3)Phi_c(g3-g1) in Fourier form with u_w in supp(phi_w^2) = [-lambda_w/2, lambda_w/2] in Montgomery alpha-units (this normalization is fixed by the pair case: tr G^2 has kernel Phi^2 with support [-lambda, lambda], matching 'bandwidth one = |alpha| <= 1'). The frequency hitting zero-ordinate g1 is xi_1 = u_a - u_c, similarly xi_2 = u_b - u_a, xi_3 = u_c - u_b; so |xi_1| <= (lambda_a + lambda_c)/2. For (0.98, 0.5, 0.5): max|xi_1| = 0.74, max|xi_2| = 0.74, max|xi_3| = 0.5 -- no direction near 1. Reaching one direction at ~1 requires lambda_a + lambda_c ~ 2, which under sigma < 2 forces lambda_b ~ 0, i.e. triples like (0.99, 0.01, 0.99) where the middle window sees primes only up to T^{0.01} -- a near-degenerate factor. Two consequences. (i) The advertised corner 'one factor at full pair bandwidth with two substantive companions' does not exist; the accessible corner has one nearly-arithmetic-free window. (ii) The correct general statement, which I verified, is: for a target frequency point (xi_1,xi_2,xi_3) on the hyperplane, the minimal window sum needed is sigma_min = sum|xi_i| (solve u_a - u_c = xi_1 etc., center at the median: min_c 2*sum|u_i - c| = 2*(max u - min u) = sum|xi_i|). Hence the union of mixed-window boxes over sigma < 2 is EXACTLY the open RS simplex {sum|xi_i| < 2} -- the thesis survives in corrected form, and this also reconciles the artifact's two seemingly inconsistent statements (7.5(e): unconditional crude MV needs 3*lambda < 2 per equal-window triple; 7.5(g): RS/Hejhal triple correlation available for lambda < 1, since equal-window kernel support is 2*lambda). REPAIR: restate the mechanism with sigma_min = sum|xi_i|, fix the example, and have the M1 LP price the actual accessible box family (products of three intervals in u-space), not the abstract simplex -- the binding rows may sit at points requiring a near-trivial window, which changes what T1 must deliver.

findings.claim: Lemma C (rank_trace_cubic) is substantially harder than the proposal's 'single genuinely new piece of linear algebra' framing admits: the mixed triple trace is not an odd moment of any single Hermitian matrix, the formalized Schur-Jensen pillar does not cover it, and the 7.5(g) proof-of-concept depends on positive semidefiniteness that fails exactly when Q is nonempty.
findings.argument: Four gaps. (i) Non-Hermitian product: tr(G_a G_b G_c) with three distinct Hermitian G's satisfies conj(tr(G_aG_bG_c)) = tr(G_aG_cG_b) != tr(G_aG_bG_c) in general; only the symmetrized real part is canonically real. All majorization/Schur-Horn/von Neumann machinery in the repo is single-matrix; there is no formalized (or paper-level) calculus for signed products of three non-commuting indefinite compressions. 7.5(g) (full-map.md line 95) is single-window tr H^3 with H = M^{1/2} Gamma M^{1/2} >= 0 under RH. (ii) The PSD hypothesis is load-bearing twice: the Lean lemma sum_gc_diag_le_sum_gc_eigenvalues (RankTraceMult.lean:119) requires M.PosSemidef, and 7.5(g)'s convex-majorization step uses f(x) = x^3/18 - x^2/9 which is convex only for x >= 2/3; with Q nonempty the spectrum contains large NEGATIVE eigenvalues (hyperbolic blocks at depth y have eigenvalues ~ +-X^{lambda y}) where f is concave -- the majorization inequality direction breaks and must be replaced by exactly the interaction-remainder accounting R that the proposal defers. (iii) The odd-trace near-cancellation is real but subtler than stated: for an isolated block with eigenvalues s/2 +- m (s = block trace asymmetry, m ~ ||u||*||v||), tr B^3 = 2s'^3 + 6s'm^2-type, i.e. it grows like (asymmetry)*X^{2*lambda*y}, and the per-block asymmetry s ~ l*Phi_w(i(2beta-1)) is itself of size X^{lambda y} -- NOT O(1). What saves validity is a sign observation the proposal never makes explicit: s has deterministic positive sign because Phi_w(iy) = integral of phi_w^2 * e^{yu} du > 0, so with c3 <= 0 isolated deep blocks strictly DECREASE the certificate's left side (validity-safe, value-costly). The un-saved part is precisely the cross terms tr(P^2Q), tr(PQ^2) and inter-block products, where relative phases oscillate and no sign is forced -- the same interaction mechanism that killed per-pair quadratic pricing at order 2 (G1-G4). The Monte Carlo gate (numerics B) is the right mitigation and the proposal deserves credit for measuring before proving, but the Lean hook's claim that the skeleton 'already covers cubic g' is half-false: sum_eigenvalues_comm is indeed general (arbitrary g with g(0)=0, verified at RankTraceMult.lean:189), but the Schur-Jensen lemma is formalized ONLY for the specific quadratic-type function gc and PSD matrices -- extending it is real new formal and mathematical work. M3 is the miracle step; I would price its success at ~0.3, well below the ambient optimism.

findings.claim: The 'free by-product' -- pair-only LP dual closing the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap -- conflates LP value-optimality with certificate validity; nothing in the existing machinery can validate an arbitrary dual weight r.
findings.argument: Theorem D is proved optimal within 'block structure + two traces + primes up to T' via [CCLM17 Cor 14] (full-map.md line 75: 'no window does better'), so any certificate exceeding 0.6725 within bandwidth one necessarily uses a functional format for which NO analytic realization currently exists -- the map's transcript hook says exactly this ('richer functionals of bandwidth-one data'). The LP dual at N=128 produces candidate weights (c0, r) that are optimal against the FEASIBLE SET of the LP, but certificate validity is the zero-side inequality 'c0 + sum_j S(j/N) r(j/N) <= p for every admissible configuration', which for the paper's certificates is supplied by Lemma 3.2 + window structure, not by the LP. The Lean Stability/RowCert harness verifies VALUES against a fixed law (lean:ceiling section: 'no formalized matching certificate ... that bridge is a paper-level remark'), not validity for zeta. So the by-product is: candidate weights plus a two-sided numerical gap -- genuinely useful, but 'closing the gap' requires a new validity lemma of unknown difficulty. The milestone text should say so.

findings.claim: M4's simple-zero payoff (delta_s > 0, stretch delta_s > 0.0094) is the least-supported number in the ladder, and the LP's binding triple rows will plausibly concentrate at the simplex edge where T1 degrades -- so realizable payoff is likely systematically below p0^(3).
findings.argument: (i) The only existence proof that a third trace buys anything (7.5(g), +0.0146) is for the DISTINCT count N_d, under RH, with Q empty; the transcript's Theorem U (full-map.md line 166) shows the odd moment adds nothing to the [0,infinity)-count/Christoffel route absent Lindelof-strength lambda_max control. The proposal's evasion (integrality atoms + the 1_{m=1} term + mixed windows, outside Theorem U's continuous-spectrum LP-dual) is legitimate but means the ENTIRE simple-count payoff rests on the M1 computation; the 'predicted range 0.69-0.73' has no calculation behind it. (ii) Structural worry not listed in the failure modes: at order 2 the 256-law's whole advantage was the FREE EDGE row j = N (edge atom mass 0.826; lean:ceiling: 'the LP's entire advantage lives in the free row j = N'). By the same mechanism, the order-3 LP's binding constraints will likely sit near the simplex boundary j1 + j2 = N, exactly where T1's error terms blow up (endpoint sigma -> 2, loglog/log losses) and where realizing the kernel requires a near-degenerate window (finding 2). REPAIR: run M1 additionally with triple rows restricted to j1 + j2 <= (1-eps)N for eps in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} and report p0^(3)(eps); if the gain evaporates for small edge retreats, the analytic program is moot and this is discovered for the price of a few LP solves.

findings.claim: M6's Alternative-Hypothesis refutation may have prior art in the point-process literature; the claim 'first test of AH against 3-level data' needs a literature check before being advertised.
findings.argument: GLSS arXiv:2507.06823 is pair-only (consistent with the proposal), but there exist constructions of full AH-compatible POINT PROCESSES (Tao's 'alternative hypothesis' construction, and related work by Lagarias-Rodgers on differences), and it is not known to this referee whether any of them is proved consistent with restricted-range 3-level correlations. Two branches: if such a process exists matching triple data on the simplex, M6's refutation hope is dead (and the M1 LP will find the corresponding law -- cheap discovery, good design); if not, the M1 LP result would be genuinely new. Either way the proposal's phrasing 'potential first refutation of AH from provable-range data' is acceptable as exploratory, but the write-up must check the AH point-process literature first. Related credit: the observation that AH's rigid half-integer spacings should generate in-band triple resonances j1+j2=j3 is plausible and concrete.
