But the true zero side is Sigma_rho h_{a,w}(gamma^W_rho); for an FE-pair at depth beta > a the pair-symmetrized value is Int hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} cosh((beta-1/2)u) e^{i gamma u} du, whose u>0 branch is e^{(beta-a)u} + e^{-(a+beta-1)u}, whereas the proposal's signed-Poisson pair value has u>0 branch -e^{-(beta-a)u} + e^{-(a+beta-1)u}. The difference is 2*cosh((beta-a)u): the true identity carries a ghost term 2*m_rho * Int_0^{log X} hat-w(u) cosh((beta-a)u) cos(gamma u + phase) du of magnitude ~ hat-w(log X) * X^{beta-a} per off-line zero. This is precisely the X^{|2beta-1|} termwise blow-up / visibility wall recorded in the canon ('the zero-side second moment cannot be read termwise'). Consequences: (a) the claim 'the windowed tilted explicit formula IS prime-computable' (Novelty section, inverting tx_048's negative finding) is false unconditionally — it is prime-computable exactly when quasi-RH(a) already holds in the window; (b) 'locality is cheap: t-resolution of width 1 needs only X ~ e^{2pi} ~ 535' conflates window resolution with detection: certifying absence of off-line zeros at height T requires the ghost to be visible, i.e. X ≳ T^c (consistent with the campaign's measured annihilation threshold L*_ann ~ 1.12 log(t0/2pi)^{0.89}), the same T^lambda economy as the two-thirds method; (c) Milestone M3's headline certificate ('no zeros with beta > 0.9, |t| <= 10^3, from primes < 10^4 alone') and the numerics-plan LP are UNSOUND as designed: they impose the ghost-free identity as a constraint on candidate configurations, which is not the true constraint satisfied by off-line configurations, so any 'certificate' so derived proves nothing; and the planned 10-digit numerical validation would pass (RH is true at tested heights, no ghost present), giving false confidence in a false identity. The formula is repairable only by reinstating the ghost — at which point the 'field' is the classical band-limited Weil EF with a tilted test family, and every escape claim built on the formula collapses.

findings.claim: The claimed new data coordinate ('depth/sigma-profiles, entirely transverse to the t-frequency form factor that all bandwidth ceilings live on') does not exist: every prime-computable observable of the field is contained in the classical band-limited Weil-EF data class, and the depth-CM generator G2 is information-free.
findings.argument: Containment: as shown in Finding 1, the tilted observable at every level a and window w with cutoff X equals the classical Weil EF evaluated at the test h_{a,w}(r) = (1/2)Int hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} e^{iru} du, which is analytic in the strip with transform supported in [-log X, log X] — a member of the standard test class with bandwidth log X. Varying a does not enlarge the class: the a-dependence enters only through the known multiplier e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} applied to the same band. So the entire (a, w)-family of prime-computable tilted-EF data at cutoff X is a SUBSET of the classical bandwidth-log X explicit-formula data — the exact data class for which the canon's obstructions (DH/Epstein satisfy the EF; o(N)/visibility blindness; adversarial configuration matching) were formulated. The genuinely new objects of the field — pointwise u(s), exact kappa_a, plume geometry — are NOT prime-computable (they require unbounded frequencies, i.e. Riemann-Siegel evaluation, as tx_048 already recorded for the K_a compressions). G2 vacuity: the 'depth-direction complete monotonicity' constraint says the prime side a |-> Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) hat-g(log n) n^{-a} is a finite totally monotone exponential sum. But this function is COMPLETELY KNOWN (finitely many known coefficients Lambda(n)hat-g(log n), known exponents log n); its total monotonicity is automatic from Lambda >= 0 and carries zero information about zeros — the whole a-family {G(a)} is generated by the single finite data vector {Lambda(n)hat-g(log n) : n <= X} under known linear maps, so 'Hausdorff-Bernstein-Widder moment constraints rigidly coupling depth profiles across all a simultaneously' constrain candidate zero configurations through exactly the same finite band-limited data a single level reads. Equivalently: for any candidate configuration, the (ghost-corrected) zero side is analytic in a, so the constraint at all a follows from the constraint near a = 2 by analytic continuation — no new equations. The S5-bandwidth evasion ('TRP certificates read a coordinate that model does not parametrize') is therefore false for everything the method can actually compute from primes; what escapes the PairCeiling format (pointwise positivity of u) escapes it only because it is not computable from the arithmetic input at all. The single-off-line-zero sensitivity (S2 evasion) is a property of the TARGET u > 0, not of any prime-computable instrument: at height T with cutoff X, a single off-line zero perturbs every computable observable by O(hat-w-weighted X^{beta-a} * oscillatory) against ambient fluctuations, invisible below the annihilation threshold — o(N)-blindness reappears exactly where it always was.

findings.claim: The index ladder kappa_a and the whole Pontryagin/OS_kappa defect layer are unconditionally ill-defined below a = 1: kappa_a may be infinite for every a in (1/2,1), and the planned Davenport-Heilbronn validation model (Milestone M2) provably has kappa = infinity at rung one, so no nontrivial finite-defect instance exists.
findings.argument: Krein-Langer theory (generalized Schur functions, Pontryagin spaces Pi_kappa) requires FINITELY many negative squares. kappa_a = #{rho : beta > a} with multiplicity. Unconditionally, finiteness of this count is open for EVERY a < 1: the best zero-density bounds (Guth-Maynard N(sigma,T) << T^{30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)}) allow the count up to height T to grow like a positive power of T at every fixed sigma < 1, and the VK zero-free region does not cover any fixed sigma < 1 at large heights. So the 'integer-valued, nonincreasing' ladder with 'jumps = multiplicities' is unconditionally defined only at a >= 1 (where it is 0); at every rung a in (1/2,1), even WELL-DEFINEDNESS (finiteness) is an unproven quasi-RH-type statement, and the OS_kappa axiom 'under kappa_a = k > 0 a k-dimensional defect space' has no known instance with 0 < k < infinity for any relevant L-function. Worse, M2 plans to 'validate the axioms on Davenport-Heilbronn as an indefinite model with kappa > 0 at rung one': the DH function has INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (classical — Titchmarsh §10.25; one zero in the half-plane of almost periodicity plus Bohr almost-periodicity/Rouché forces infinitude; same for Epstein zetas with h > 1). So DH's K_a has infinitely many negative squares at a = 1: it is not a Pontryagin model at rung one, and the planned validation is impossible as stated. Additionally the proposal itself flags (failure mode iv) that even the bounded-type hypothesis for Theta_a = xi(1-a-iz)/xi(a-iz) is unverified (xi has order 1 but infinite exponential type; bounded type of the ratio in C+ needs proof). Combined with Finding 2, BOTH advertised 'new generators' (G1 Pontryagin-RP bookkeeping, G2 depth-CM) are stripped: what remains of the OS layer under TRP(a) is the Herglotz/Poisson representation of a positive harmonic function — classical, and the proposal's own failure mode 2 concedes the layer may be 'decorative'.

findings.claim: The central wager (margin propagation, M4) is a known-hard problem in disguise, and a Beurling-type barrier world shows the field's axiom system as designed cannot power it: any inequality derivable from OS_kappa + depth-CM alone is violated by Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer configurations, so M4 must consume an input the axioms do not encode.
findings.argument: Hidden hardness (partly admitted by the proposal, failure mode 1): the ambient archimedean level of u at height t is ~(1/2)log(t/2pi), and pointwise positivity near a = 1/2 must beat Re zeta'/zeta oscillations of size ~log t, while the band-limited prime side controls only the smoothed component; controlling the unsmoothed remainder on windows of length ~1/log T is precisely the campaign's 'Lindelof lock' (bounds for P_X on windows of length 1/log T), never attacked successfully. Any nontrivial m(a-eps,T) >= phi(m(a,T),...) iterates to new zero-free regions, i.e. is at least as hard as improving Vinogradov-Korobov (unimproved since 1958); the designer's own probability is 0.1. Barrier sketch: the generators as axiomatized consume Lambda >= 0, Hadamard/harmonic structure, rung-one positivity, and the FE only structurally (pairing/unimodularity) — no quantitative archimedean-vs-prime rigidity and no integer/exponential-sum structure. Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (2006) constructed Beurling generalized-prime systems with Lambda_B >= 0, Chebyshev-type prime counting, analytic continuation in a region, AND zeros essentially filling a dlVP-shaped boundary curve — showing that Lambda >= 0 + one-line positivity + harmonic-function machinery alone cannot push the zero-free region below the classical shape. Caveat stated honestly: DMV systems lack a functional equation and entirety, so this is a barrier against the AXIOM SYSTEM (OS-Schwarz + Poisson semigroup + CM prime side, which apply verbatim in the DMV region of continuation), not a strict RH-false lookalike for the full input list; but it proves M2's kill criterion ('at least one inequality not derivable from classical harmonic-function theory') must fail unless the axioms are extended by exactly the quantitative FE/integer input (VK exponential-sum technology) whose absence the proposal advertises as elegance. The residual honest reading — 'an elegant RP-reformulation of Vinogradov-Korobov' — is the proposal's own words for its main failure mode.

findings.claim: The headline numerical evidence ('margin law m(a,60) ~ 0.046(a-1/2), linear in depth exactly as the ladder predicts') is a low-t boundary artifact carrying no information about propagation structure.
findings.argument: The infimum of u(a+it) over t in (1,60) is attained at the bottom edge t ~ 1, where ALL zeros are far (first ordinate 14.13) and u(a+i*1) ~ 2(a-1/2) Sigma_gamma gamma^{-2} = 2(a-1/2)(0.02310) = 0.0462(a-1/2) — reproducing the reported 0.0464(a-1/2) to the digit. This is the Lagarias identity evaluated at one uninteresting point: linearity in (a-1/2) is trivial (every term is proportional to it when |t-gamma| >> a-1/2), and the coefficient is just 2*Sigma gamma^{-2}. It says nothing about the structure of m(a,T) where the ladder's difficulty lives (between-zero minima at large heights, where gaps ~2pi/log T and plumes of hypothetical off-line zeros sit). Presenting it as 'exactly as the ladder predicts' is numerology; the honest check (the proposal's own planned Margin Atlas at T up to 10^4) would reveal the inf stays pinned at the low-t edge.

findings.claim: The first theorem is probably true but its sketch constants fail as stated, and its novelty is modest: it is classical partial fractions plus effective Riemann-von Mangoldt, with unacknowledged prior art on the u > 0 reformulation itself.
findings.argument: (1) Constants: the sketch takes windows of length H0 ~ 1.5 around t0 and claims >= c0 log t0 zeros for |t0| >= 30 via Trudgian-type S(t) bounds. With main term (3/2pi)log(t0/2pi) ~ 0.477 log t0 against S-variation up to ~0.224 log t0 + 0.556 loglog t0 + ~6.8, the guaranteed count is NEGATIVE until log t0 ~ 30+, i.e. t0 ~ 10^13. Repairable by taking H0 ~ 30 (count positive at t0 = 30, per-zero contribution weakens by ~H0^2, inflating C1 accordingly) or by verified computation at low heights — the theorem survives with uglier constants, as failure mode 5 half-anticipates. (2) Novelty: the contrapositive is a quantitative form of the classical Landau partial-fraction lemma (zeta'/zeta(s) = Sigma_{|rho-s|<1} 1/(s-rho) + O(log t)) plus a two-sided RvM window count; assembling it with explicit constants is a publishable note, not a cornerstone. The underlying reformulation (RH iff Re xi'/xi > 0 for sigma > 1/2; unconditional on sigma >= 1) has prior art beyond Lagarias 1999 that the proposal's novelty section misses: Sondow-Dumitrescu 2010 ('A monotonicity property of Riemann's xi function and a reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis') and Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski on horizontal monotonicity of |xi| — so 'no publication studies the geometry of {Re xi'/xi <= 0}' is overstated (the plume/anchoring GEOMETRY may be unstudied, but the positivity reformulation is established folklore). Also minor: the 'Lean-verified first rung' is Re xi'/xi >= N_T/(8t^2) only for sigma in [1,2] AND |t| >= max(2, 2T) (ZeroFree.lean:396), not the full ray a >= 1 as the thesis line implies.

verdicts.repairs: The direction is not salvageable as a 'new field', but four pieces survive if rebuilt honestly. (1) Restate the master formula correctly: derive the tilted EF AS a classical Weil EF with test h_{a,w}(r) = (1/2)Int hat-w(u)e^{-(a-1/2)|u|}e^{iru}du, including the off-line ghost term 2m_rho Int hat-w(u)cosh((beta-a)u)cos(gamma u)du; state explicitly that the ghost-free form at level a is EQUIVALENT to quasi-RH(a) in the window. All downstream claims ('prime-computable with tiny cutoffs', M3 boxes, the LP experiment) must then be redesigned as dichotomy/visibility arguments importing the L*_ann threshold, accepting X ~ T^c scaling — at which point compare honestly against Riemann-Siegel direct verification (Platt-Trudgian 3*10^12), which currently dominates every low-height box certificate. (2) Keep M1 (anchoring theorem) as a standalone note: fix H0 (take H0 ~ 30 or split off a verified-computation region), use Trudgian's actual constants, cite Sondow-Dumitrescu and Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski as prior art, and position T1 (positivity on the VK region) as a corollary-level observation. (3) Drop the Pontryagin/kappa_a layer or condition every statement on the (open) finiteness hypothesis kappa_a < infinity; replace the DH validation model with finite truncations or artificial finite-index models, since DH and Epstein h>1 have infinitely many zeros in sigma > 1. (4) Convert Finding 2 into the field's one genuinely valuable theorem — the calibrator the proposal promises as milestone 3: a formal proof that the full (a,w)-family of prime-computable tilted-EF observables at cutoff X is contained in the classical bandwidth-log X Weil-EF data class, i.e. a depth-direction analogue of the bandwidth-one ceiling delimiting exactly which depth data any future method must consume. That negative result is publishable, formalizable on the existing Lean seams, and is the honest deliverable of this design. Before any M4 attempt, the axiom system must be extended by an input that Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer Beurling worlds violate (quantitative FE rigidity or integer exponential-sum structure); absent that, M4 is a reformulation of Vinogradov-Korobov.
literature_flags: Lagarias, Acta Arith. 89 (1999): exact statement of unconditional positivity on Re s >= 1 and the RH-equivalence — load-bearing for the first theorem; verify (likely correct).

Trudgian's explicit S(t) bound: proposal quotes |S(t)| <= 0.112 log t + 0.278 loglog t + 3.385; Trudgian 2014 gives constant 2.510, later refinements differ — the exact constants are load-bearing for the anchoring sketch and its H0 failure threshold.

Krein-Langer applicability to Theta_a: requires BOTH bounded type in C+ (unproven for xi-ratios; xi is order 1 but infinite exponential type) AND finitely many negative squares — the latter is an open quasi-RH-type statement for every a < 1; the proposal flags only the former.

Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 / Titchmarsh §10.25: DH has INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (Bohr almost-periodicity); same for Epstein h > 1 — this contradicts M2's 'DH as indefinite model with kappa > 0' (kappa is infinite, not positive-finite).

Missing prior art on the positivity reformulation: Sondow-Dumitrescu 2010 (arXiv:1005.1104) and Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski (horizontal monotonicity of |xi|) — the novelty claim 'no publication studies {Re xi'/xi <= 0}' is overstated.

Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh arXiv:2306.04799 (complex-zero form factor, |alpha| < 1): the tilted-EF data family lands inside exactly this data class — relevant when formalizing the containment theorem proposed as a repair.

findings.claim: The headline thesis deliverable — 'the first depth-resolved UNCONDITIONAL constraints on off-line zeros of zeta' (M2) — is not deliverable unconditionally: the required per-pair survival lower bound needs local zero-density control at scale a/log T that is exactly the campaign's Lindelof-lock / visibility-wall territory, and no unconditional input closes the gap.
findings.argument: The M2 transfer needs a survival LOWER bound: a zeta pair at depth a/L (z-height y=2a/L) must remain a complex zero of H_t until t ~ sigma_death*4/L^2, so that the forward complex-pair count bound p(sigma) <= (J_+(sigma)/2)N catches it. The zero velocity under dH/dt = -H'' is zdot_j = 2*sum_{k!=j} 1/(z_j - z_k); every real zero contributes a strictly DOWNWARD vertical component -2y/|z-x_k|^2 on a complex zero (real zeros accelerate death, never delay it). A survival bound therefore requires an upper bound on sum_k 2y/(d_k^2+y^2), i.e. on the number of zeros within horizontal distance ~y = 2a/L of the pair, along the whole flow trajectory (zeros of H_{t'}, 0<=t'<=t, not just of zeta). Unconditionally we only have N(t+1)-N(t) << log t = L, which permits ~L zeros inside the width-(2a/L) window beneath the pair; that gives downward velocity up to ~2L/y = L^2/a and survival only sigma >~ a^2/L -> 0 — vacuous. Closing the gap needs #{zeros in windows of width a/L} <= C*a pointwise, i.e. short-window zero-counting at scale 1/log T — precisely the scale the parent's map flags as Lindelof-type information (the orthonormalization block: 'bounds for P_X on windows of length 1/log T'; unconditional S(t)=O(log t) is the wall). This is the dynamical reincarnation of the Part-I interference/visibility wall ('no configuration-free visibility theorem exists'): the proposal's evasion of formalized depth-blindness — 'depth is priced through TIME OF SURVIVAL' — reintroduces per-configuration cluster sensitivity at exactly the point where the campaign proved such configuration-free lemmas empty. The proposal's own failure-mode #3 concedes the risk, but its fallback ('zeta transfer under a mild local-density hypothesis') is near-circular: bounding hypothetical deep zeros requires assuming the very off-line/near-line zeros being bounded do not cluster, an assumption of unknown status that is itself bandwidth-invisible. What survives unconditionally is only the H_t-side complex-zero count p(sigma) <= (J_+(sigma)/2)N — a statement about H_t with no zeta content. The thesis clause 'convert the parent method's provable depth-blindness into the first depth-resolved unconditional constraints on off-line zeros of zeta' is therefore refuted as stated.

findings.claim: Even granting a local-density hypothesis, the M2 depth dictionary sigma_death ~ a^2/2 is wrong at leading order for all a >~ 1-2: the collective attraction of the real-zero lattice dominates the conjugate attraction, the true dictionary is asymptotically LINEAR in a, and the quoted numbers (0.0317N at a=3, 0.0041N at a=5, tail ~2N/a^4) are unobtainable by this mechanism.
findings.argument: The isolated-pair law y(t)^2 = y(0)^2 - 2t (whence sigma_death = a^2/2) keeps only the conjugate term -1/y in dy/dt. But the embedded pair also feels the real lattice: with mean gap g = 4pi/L and generic (mid-gap) position, sum_{k in Z} 2y/(((k+1/2)g)^2 + y^2) = (2pi/g)*tanh(pi*y/g), giving ratio (lattice force)/(conjugate force) = a*tanh(a/2) with a = yL/2. Verified numerically: ratio = 0.46 at a=1, 2.72 at a=3, 4.93 at a=5 — the lattice term DOMINATES at the proposal's own quoted depths (a=3,5 correspond to y/g = 0.48, 0.80, i.e. order-one fractions of a mean gap; this is a mean-field effect of the generic lattice, not exceptional 'clusters'). Integrating the corrected ODE, sigma_death(a) = int_0^a s ds/(1 + s*tanh(s/2)): sigma_death(3) = 1.97 vs claimed 4.5; sigma_death(5) = 3.62 vs claimed 12.5; asymptotically sigma_death ~ a - O(log a), linear (hydrodynamic constant-speed descent dy/dt = -2*pi*rho = -L/2, since the vertical Poisson-kernel integral against a uniform density is y-independent). The resulting corrected bounds are J_+(1.97)/2 = 0.078 (2.5x weaker than the claimed 0.0317) at a=3, J_+(3.62)/2 = 0.043 (10x weaker than 0.0041) at a=5, and tail ~c/a^2 instead of 2/a^4. Screening (the pair repels nearby real zeros, opening a cavity) cannot restore a^2/2: over the death timescale real zeros move only ~0.6 mean gaps, and the far-field half of the drift, 2*int_y^inf rho*(2y/r^2) dr = 4*rho ~ 0.3L, comes from |x'-x| > y and is unremovable by any local rearrangement, so sigma_death <= C*a with C ~ 2 robustly. Consequence: the quantitative depth-resolved curve in the immutable Mechanism and Payoff sections is wrong at leading order wherever it claims new content beyond a ~ 1, and the weaker ~N/a^2 curve loses to Selberg-type near-line density bounds N e^{-ca} at much smaller depths, further shrinking the novelty window (a comparison the proposal only flags for the a^{-4} curve).

findings.claim: M3's 'genuinely open, either answer is a theorem' framing is oversold: at the level of PROVABLE transport rows the joint-sigma LP cannot lower the 0.6818 optimum, so Outcome A (breaking the bandwidth-one ceiling for zeta) is essentially foreclosed and the M3 payoff should be priced as Outcome B (a no-go extension) only.
findings.argument: Three independent structural reasons. (i) Edge invariance, conceded by the proposal: the LP value 0.68182868746 is generated entirely by the free edge row j=N (edge atom mass 0.826 at alpha=1, per the Lean map: 'The LP's entire advantage lives in the free row j = N'), and the flow multiplier e^{-2*sigma*alpha*(1-alpha)} equals 1 at alpha=1 — the binding degree of freedom is flow-invariant at every sigma. (ii) Row redundancy by universal linear response: the damped sigma-rows F_t(alpha) = |alpha|e^{-2*sigma*alpha(1-alpha)} are the linearized log-gas relaxation of density modes (damping rate proportional to alpha(1-alpha), vanishing at both ends), which depends at leading order only on the pair data itself; any near-equilibrium adversary (the 256-law is within 3e-40 of CUE in the open band) flows to the same damped open-band values, so the sigma>0 form-factor rows are functions of the sigma=0 rows over the adversary class, and adding functionally dependent rows cannot lower an LP optimum. The only channel by which flow rows could bite is O(1) nonlinear coupling of the edge/doubles structure into the open band — unprovable with current tools and not what the LP as specified tests. (iii) Weakness of provable transport: the LP can only impose transport facts that are theorems — forward persistence of real zeros, instantaneous splitting of real doubles (local model h = z^2 - 2t), de Bruijn strip shrink, count stability. A trivially rebuilt adversary family satisfies all of them: 256-law at sigma=0; at each sigma>0 an all-real-simple configuration matching the damped rows, with the split doubles' close-pair signature (spacing ~ sqrt(2t) ~ 0.45 mean gaps at sigma=1) hidden at frequencies alpha ~ 1/spacing > 1, ABOVE the band edge where no row constrains anything. Per-pair transport constraints strong enough to exclude this family are exactly the M2-type dynamical lemmas blocked by finding 1. Note this does not touch M3-as-computation: running the LP and getting Outcome B is still a publishable formalized no-go, but the coin-flip framing inflates the expected zeta payoff.

findings.claim: The backward branch (t < 0: certificate for sigma < sigma* = 2.657, small-gap/cluster bounds, backward strip control) has no analytic support in the cited toolkit and should be priced as unproven new territory, not 'same proof'.
findings.argument: The First-theorem section says 'Companion statement (same proof, backward)', but every effective ingredient cited is forward-only: Polymath15's A+B-C effective approximations are established for t in [0,1/2] (their entire pipeline addresses t>0; nothing exists at t<0 beyond the trivial identity H_t = Gaussian_{|t|} * H_0); the de Bruijn strip theorem (zeros in |Im z| <= sqrt(Delta^2 - 2t)) is the FORWARD direction, and the needed backward strip-growth bound |Im z| <= sqrt(1 + 2|t|) for Gaussian convolutions is recalled-unverified (the proposal itself marks the max-principle 'recalled, verify') yet is load-bearing for the ZeroConfig instantiation at t<0 (the '|y| <= 1 + O(sigma/L^2) harmless in the X^{1/2}-tail' claim). The backward effective explicit formula — extracting Lambda(n)e^{+sigma*alpha(1-alpha)} coefficients with errors o(main) at bandwidth ~1 from the convolution representation — is a genuinely new analytic development with amplified (e^{sigma/4}) coefficients thinning the endpoint margins that the parent's Remark 6.1 already calls delicate. Since the backward certificate, the small-gap corollary, and half the equivalence ladder consume it, roughly half of M1-M2's advertised statement types rest on undeveloped analysis. Not fatal (the forward branch stands on Polymath15 + the verified multiplier), but the two-year first-theorem confidence of 0.65 should attach to the forward branch at lambda < 1 only.

findings.claim: The claimed dynamical breaking of the lemmaR_tight degeneracy ('the sigma-derivative of the certificate family separates configurations that any single-sigma certificate provably cannot') has no unconditional cash value: the provable half of the separation generates no certifiable constraint, and the informative half is the blocked survival lemma.
findings.argument: The degeneracy is on-line double (price 4) vs depth->0 off-line pair (price 4). Under forward flow the double splits into two real simples — this direction IS provable (instantaneous splitting + forward realness persistence). But all sigma>0 certificate outputs are LOWER bounds on real-simple fractions, which an adversary whose doubles have split satisfies trivially; splitting therefore never produces a violated constraint. The only upper-bound object in the family is the complex-pair count p(sigma) <= (J_+(sigma)/2)N, and routing the deep-pair side of the degeneracy through it requires the per-pair survival lower bound blocked by finding 1. So at the level of provable statements the flow family separates the two configurations in exactly zero certifiable directions; the 'uncountable family of instantiations' adds genuinely new certified numbers about H_t, but the degeneracy-breaking claim against the formalized tightness theorem is, unconditionally, empty.

findings.claim: M4's equivalence [diffusive flow-realness for all sigma] <=> [narrow-box hypothesis] is doubly conditional: the reverse direction is 'modulo M2' (blocked per finding 1), and even the forward direction (NB => flow-realness) needs a localized/windowed de Bruijn strip theorem that does not follow verbatim from the global one.
findings.argument: The global de Bruijn theorem assumes ALL zeros in a strip of width Delta and shrinks the whole strip; NB gives depth o(1/log T) — a height-DEPENDENT strip (Delta(T) = o(1/log T)), to which the global theorem does not apply since sup_T Delta(T)*anything is realized at low heights where depths can be large. The flow is nonlocal (H_t(z) depends on all of H_0), so 'complex pairs in the window (T,2T] die by t ~ 2*delta^2' requires a windowed death-time upper bound with control of the influence of out-of-window zeros — plausible via localized harmonic-measure/Rouche arguments but a new lemma, not a citation. Since the proposal advertises M4 as 'the flow separates RH into a diffusive layer (attackable, NB-equivalent) and a fixed-t layer', both halves of the separation carry unproven dynamical lemmas; the stratification is a conjecture-shaped picture, not a near-theorem. (The proposal's own text does say '(c) modulo the M2 survival lemma' — this finding records that the OTHER direction also has a gap.)

verdicts.repairs: The salvage is substantial because the core engine verified. (1) Record the multiplier as VERIFIED, not at-risk: Polymath15's B_t coefficient exponent e^{(t/16)log^2(x/(4 pi n^2))}, taken relative to n=1, equals e^{(t/4) log n (log n - L')} with L' = log(x/4pi) — exactly the proposal's m_n; failure-mode #1's 'reconciliation did not close' now closes, and the numerics kill-switch becomes confirmation rather than triage. (2) Restate M2 honestly as two results: (a) unconditional complex-zero counts and realness/simplicity proportions for H_t itself (no zeta content, but new); (b) a CONDITIONAL zeta depth bound under an explicit no-clustering hypothesis (zeros of H_{t'} in windows of width a/log T bounded by C*a along the trajectory), with the corrected mean-field dictionary sigma_death(a) = int_0^a s ds/(1+s tanh(s/2)) (linear tail, bound ~N/a^2, not ~2N/a^4), and an honest comparison window against Selberg/Jutila near-line density bounds N e^{-ca}. Kill the word 'unconditional' in the thesis's depth-resolved clause. (3) Reframe M3 around Outcome B as the deliverable: run the linear-response computation on the 256-law FIRST (cheap) to confirm row redundancy; the one genuinely open refinement is whether O(1) nonlinear edge-mode coupling (doubles/edge atom feeding the open band at second order in the flow) is computable and provable — state that as the only channel to Outcome A. (4) Demote the backward branch to a separate milestone gated on deriving an effective t<0 approximation and verifying the backward strip-growth theorem; let M1 = forward branch at fixed lambda < 1 (as the mitigation already suggests). (5) Keep M5 as scoped — PaperInputsFlow mirrors the PaperInputs pattern and is cheap; it is the strongest surviving payoff line together with the flowed-BGSTB form factor.
literature_flags: Polymath15 (arXiv:1904.12438) B_t effective approximation: verify the coefficient exponent shape e^{(t/16)log^2(x/(4 pi n^2))} and normalization conventions (their x vs the proposal's z, factors of 2/4); my reconciliation closes the proposal's flagged gap but was done from a recalled exponent — also confirm uniformity of their error terms as t -> 0 (they work at fixed t in [0,1/2]).

de Bruijn 1950 (Thm 13): forward strip-shrink |Im z| <= sqrt(Delta^2 - 2t) — recalled, verify statement and hypotheses; separately verify whether a backward strip-GROWTH bound |Im z| <= sqrt(Delta^2 + 2|t|) for Gaussian convolution is actually a theorem (load-bearing for the t<0 ZeroConfig instantiation; I could only confirm it on the toy example z^2 + eps^2).

Ki-Kim-Lee 2009 (Adv. Math.): confirm no quantitative small-t uniformity (e.g. #nonreal zeros of H_t << exp(c/sqrt(t)) concentrated below height exp(c/sqrt(t))) that would partially trivialize the windowed forward claims; the structure (fixed-t exceptional zeros live at heights where t*log^2(height) = O(1), i.e. below T^{c/sqrt(sigma)}) supports the proposal's novelty claim but should be checked against KKL's actual error terms and successors.

Near-line zero-density constants: Selberg 1946 N(1/2 + delta, T) << T^{1 - c*delta} log T — verify the value of c and the modern best (Jutila, Conrey, Watt, Guth-Maynard-adjacent) at depth a/log T; this sets the honest crossover depth beyond which any flow-derived depth bound (a^{-2} or a^{-4} curve alike) is dominated by classical results.

Goldston-Suriajaya narrow-box papers (arXiv:2603.28104, arXiv:2501.14545): check whether unconditional depth-resolved bounds at scale a/log T already exist there — direct competitors to the M2 corollary that the proposal only 'flags for verification'.

Rodgers-Tao (Forum Math Pi 2020): verify their t<0 mechanism produces a positive PROPORTION of complex zeros in dyadic windows at diffusive backward times t = -Theta(1/log^2 T) (the proposal's backward-branch framing and consistency check (i) both assume the quantitative form of their contradiction).

Zero-counting for H_t: verify N_t(T,2T) = N(T,2T)(1 + O(sigma/L)) against Polymath15's N_t asymptotics (the flow adds terms ~(t/16)log^2-type to the counting function; the proposal flags this and only needs o(N), but the flag should be discharged).

findings.claim: Lemma C's sign-indefinite cross term tr(P^2 Q) re-opens the lambda_max/Lindelof branch of the recorded odd-moment no-go (transcript p.80, tx_081), which the proposal's obstruction-evasion section never addresses; the stated remainder form R <= eps*tr A^2 + C(eps)*(trace-asymmetry) does not cover it in the intermediate-depth regime.
findings.argument: tx_081 states the no-go in two parts: (a) an LP certificate p(mu)=c1 mu+c2 mu^2+c3 mu^3 <= 1 on (0,inf) needs c3<=0 and is then dominated by its quadratic part; (b) 'the third moment would help only together with an a-priori bound lambda_max(R~)=O(1), i.e. a pointwise bound for Sum_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-1/2-i tau} on windows of length 1/L' — Lindelof-strength. The proposal evades (a) legitimately (integer-multiplicity cubic via majorization is outside the eigenvalue-valid class; 7.5(g) proves cubic beats quadratic under RH). It never mentions (b). Audit of rank_trace_cubic: with c3<=0, expand tr A^3 = tr P^3 + 3tr(P^2Q) + 3tr(PQ^2) + tr Q^3. tr(PQ^2)>=0 (both PSD) enters with favorable sign c3<0. tr Q^3: I VERIFIED the proposal's odd-trace near-cancellation claim — for a pair block 2m(xx^T-yy^T) with u=x+iy the evaluation vector, ||x||^2-||y||^2 = Re(sum_k u_k^2), and the sub-critical Gabor-Poisson identity gives sum_k phihat(g-tau_k)^2 = l*(phi*phi)(0) EXACTLY for all complex g (the m>=1 aliasing samples of phi*phi at +-l vanish for lambda_w<=1), so the per-block trace asymmetry is O(m*l), depth-independent and sign-definite; hence tr B^3 ~ 3 mu^2 * asym with asym = +2ml*int(phi^2) > 0, and c3<=0 makes tr Q^3 favorable too. The residual danger is exactly tr(P^2 Q) = sum_blocks 2m(||Px||^2 - ||Py||^2): sign-indefinite (no Poisson rigidity — it equals Re sum_{j,j'} m_j m_{j'} <v_j,v_{j'}> l^2 Phi(gamma_j - g)Phi(gamma_{j'} - g), position-dependent complex phases), controllable adversarially by micro-shifting the off-line ordinate by ~pi/(lambda l) to flip the phase of Phi at complex argument. Homogeneity check of the claimed pricing: per deep block |tr(P^2 B)| ~ X^y * l^a (a>=1 from local overlaps, larger with admissible clustering N(t+1)-N(t) ~ log t giving lambda_max(P) ~ l), the block's tr A^2 contribution is ~X^{2y}, and its asymmetry is O(ml). eps*tr A^2 covers only blocks with X^y >= l^a/eps; C(eps)*asym covers only O(l) per block. The intermediate regime X^y ~ polylog with K ~ N/polylog blocks (t2 budget K*X^{2y} <= eta*N respected, remaining traces matched within the o(main) tolerances by adjusting the standard extremal background) yields total unpriced junk ~ N * l^{power} >> the certified gain delta*N. So the Lean-hook statement of rank_trace_cubic with that remainder form is very likely false against the abstract configuration class, and any repair that bounds tr(P^2 Q) for the true zeta multiset appears to need ||P||_op-type control, i.e. the short-window P_X bounds of Remark 7.1(ii) — the known-hard sub-Lindelof threshold. The cited proof-of-concept 7.5(g) is Q-EMPTY (RH-conditional), so it evidences nothing about this term. The proposal's own mitigation (numerics (b) Monte Carlo) measures typical configurations, but validity must hold configuration-by-configuration; the G1-G4 history shows exactly this typical-vs-adversarial gap being fatal. Not scored fatal only because: (i) my l-power bookkeeping in the intermediate regime is a sketch and the campaign has previously produced surprising Poisson rigidities (as with the trace asymmetry) that could yet tame Re(u^T P^2 u); (ii) the proposal gates M3/M4 behind M1+MC and its failure modes name this risk. But the burden is on the proposal: as designed, the certificate arm collides with the recorded no-go's unaddressed branch rather than evading it.

findings.claim: The headline 'mixed-window corner' novelty rests on the paper's crude equal-window accounting (k*lambda<2 => lambda<2/3 at k=3) and is contradicted by the campaign's own sharper record: tx_081 states the odd-moment Fourier support reaches (k-1)*lambda, so k=3 is 'admissible on the whole useful range' lambda<1 with EQUAL windows — the proposal never reconciles the two, and its information-region claim is not new either way.
findings.argument: Shell geometry: the triple-trace functional only probes the sum-zero shell xi1+xi2+xi3=0. For equal windows |xi_i|<=lambda, the maximum of |xi1|+|xi2|+|xi1+xi2| on the shell is 2*lambda (one coordinate must balance the other two, and |xi3|<=lambda caps the balancing), so equal windows at lambda=0.98 already access a region with total support 1.96<2 — a STRICT SUPERSET of the mixed (0.98,0.5,0.5) region, which additionally constrains |xi2|<=0.5. Hence 'one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1, a corner the equal-window analysis never touched' is false at the level of accessible support: mixed windows are a restriction, not an extension, of the equal-window region at lambda_max. What is genuinely at issue is the PROOF range: the proposal's absolute-value MV accounting needs sigma=lambda_a+lambda_b+lambda_c<2 because the far-off-diagonal (|log(n1 n2/n3)| >~ 1, suppressed only by the ~1/(y-z) Dirichlet-kernel tails of the sharp k<d grid cutoff, no rapid decay) carries ell^1 mass ~ sqrt(X_a X_b)*sqrt(X_c) = T^{sigma/2}; tx_081's lambda<1 claim for equal windows would need genuine cancellation there (or relies on its admittedly from-memory RS recall). So either (i) tx_081 is right, and the mixed-window innovation is vacuous — equal windows at lambda->1 already deliver the third trace, which is precisely the situation in which tx_081 then derived the odd-moment no-go — or (ii) the proposal's sigma<2 is the honest boundary, in which case its 'Rudnick-Sarnak boundary re-derived' framing should be presented as the absolute-value-MV boundary and the internal contradiction with the campaign record must be resolved explicitly. The surviving novelty is real but much narrower than claimed: mixed windows enlarge the achievable KERNEL CONE (products Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c with three distinct windows, useful for LP rows) within a support region that is not new.

findings.claim: M1's LP overstates the provable data class: it pins every triple row A3(j1,j2) within a uniform tolerance tau3, but T1 delivers only smooth product-kernel functionals Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c on the shell, each with its own o(1) error; the go/no-go readout p0^(3)-p0^(2)>0.02 is therefore biased toward 'go', and the M4 certificate cannot consume the rows as priced.
findings.argument: T1 (or RS-type input) yields, per window triple, ONE number: sum_{j1,j2} Phihat_a(j1)Phihat_b(j2)Phihat_c(j1+j2)-weighted combinations of the A3 observables, with an error at the theorem's o(main) scale. Recovering pointwise rows A3(j1,j2)=0 +- tau3 at all ~N^2/2 simplex points requires inverting a tensor-product-cone decomposition (delta-like kernels are not C^3-taper products; the decomposition's ell^1 coefficient mass multiplies the per-instance tolerances), so the certified tolerance at a single grid point degrades by the conditioning of that decomposition — potentially by large factors at N=64-128. An LP whose adversary must match all pointwise rows within a uniform small tau3 is strictly more constrained than one facing only the achievable cone, so p0^(3) computed as designed is an upper bound on the true worth of the upgrade, and the M1 decision gate can pass while the honest (achievable-cone) value collapses toward p0^(2). Likewise the LP dual weights may correspond to a non-achievable kernel, in which case 'the candidate optimal certificate whose validity Lemma C must prove' is not fed by T1 at all. Repair is clean and should be mandatory: parameterize LP rows by the achievable product-kernel cone (mixed windows legitimately enrich it — see finding 2) with propagated tolerances, and re-anchor the 0.02 gate on that LP.

findings.claim: The 'first unconditional correlation theorem for zeta zeros beyond order 2' headline (novelty 1, milestone M2) rests on an unverified negative claim about Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 that the campaign's own record contradicts: tx_081 recalls RS 'prove the n-level correlations are GUE for Sum|xi_j|<2 and state explicitly that RH is not assumed' for zeta.
findings.argument: If RS 1996 (Duke 81) is unconditional for zeta on the full class of test functions with hat-support in Sum|xi_j|<2 — as the tx_081 agent explicitly recalls, and as is consistent with BGSTB24 having targeted only the Montgomery-F(alpha)-specific weighted form at the pair level — then T1's content reduces to: RS's theorem + the (exact, easy) Gabor-Poisson repackaging into mixed Gram traces + explicit error terms, and both novelty claim (1) ('exists in print only under RH') and M2's standalone-headline payoff are wrong. The proposal flags this for verification but nonetheless builds its milestone-payoff structure ('standalone headline theorem... independent of the certificate program's fate') and its BGSTB-analogy framing on the unverified branch. Note the two-sided effect: if RS is unconditional the route's FEASIBILITY improves (the analytic input may be quotable rather than provable-from-scratch, de-risking M2) while the payoff collapses to a technical variant; if RS is conditional, M2 stands but the tx_081-based equal-window claim in finding 2 weakens. Either resolution materially changes the proposal's expected value, and it must be resolved (against the original paper, not memory) before any M2 spend.

findings.claim: The cited proof-of-concept (Section 7.5(g), f(x)=-x^2/9+x^3/18, N_d>=0.85082 under RH) uses the opposite certificate direction from Lemma C: convex f with c3=+1/18>0 consumed via Schur-Horn (sum f(m_j) <= tr f(A)), whereas the proposal's validity polynomial forces c3<=0 and the concave Schur-Jensen direction; 'cubic accounting survives interactions' in the convex direction is automatic majorization and is not evidence about Lemma C's actual content.
findings.argument: psi(m)=c1 m+c2 m^2+c3 m^3+c4*1_{m=1} <= 1 on all integers m>=1 forces c3<=0 (else psi->+inf), and the certificate consumes sum psi(m_j) >= trace-combo - penalties, i.e. the concave/Schur-Jensen direction (which also forces c2<=0 for concavity on [0,inf)). 7.5(g)'s f has positive cubic coefficient and is consumed in the convex/Schur-Horn direction (upper-bounding sum f(m_j) by the trace to penalize high multiplicities). For a single PSD matrix in Gram coordinates both directions are the same diagonal-vs-eigenvalue majorization fact, so the P-only 'survival of interactions' is trivial in both; everything hard in Lemma C is the Q-mixed terms (finding 1), about which 7.5(g) — being Q-empty — says nothing. The citation should be corrected from 'proof-of-concept that cubic accounting survives interactions' to 'proof that a third trace has nonzero certificate value in the Q-free case'; as written it overstates the evidential support for the route's core lemma.

findings.claim: T1's core MV mechanics are sound (verified), but the proposal's 'ratio-type frequencies are handled identically' glosses the one place its own hardest risk lives, and the same-prime-power and near-diagonal bookkeeping deserve one caveat each.
findings.argument: Verified in the proposal's favor: (i) the spacing-weighted MV norms are computed correctly — with coefficients (Lambda*Lambda)(m)/sqrt(m) and delta_m >= 1/(2m), |a_m|^2/delta_m = 2(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2, and sum_{m<=Y}(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2 ~ c Y log^3 Y (partial summation over sum_p (log p)^2/p), giving the claimed l^2 T^{sigma/2} = o(T l^3) iff sigma<2; (ii) the near-diagonal band |log(m/n3)|<=1/T is empty since the resonance forces m ~ n3 <= X_c <= T so |m-n3| <= m/T < 1; (iii) exact relations n1 n2 = n3 among prime powers force a common prime, and sum_p (log p)^3 sum_{a,b} p^{-a-b} converges — subleading as claimed; (iv) the three-fold Poisson resummation to the zero side is exact at sub-critical sampling for all lambda_w <= 1 (the aliasing samples of phi*phi at the closed endpoint +-l vanish by continuity). The caveat: the far-off-diagonal is suppressed only by first-order Dirichlet-kernel decay from the sharp k<d grid cutoff (no smooth T-taper is present in the trace), which is exactly why sigma<2 is the absolute-value boundary (finding 2) and why any endpoint improvement or the fallback erosion to sigma<3/2 would shrink both the accessible simplex and the LP value — consistent with, but sharper than, the proposal's own flagged risk.

verdicts.repairs: 1) RECONCILE WITH THE CAMPAIGN RECORD (blocks everything else): resolve the tx_081 vs sigma<2 discrepancy on the equal-window k=3 range, and resolve the unconditional status of Rudnick-Sarnak 1996 (and Hejhal 1994) against the originals before any M2 spend. If RS is unconditional for zeta, recast M2 as 'Gram-trace packaging with explicit errors, mixed-window kernel cone' (quotable input, lower risk, lower payoff) and delete 'first unconditional triple correlation' from the payoff ledger. 2) NAME THE LAMBDA_MAX LOCK AS AN OBSTRUCTION: add the second branch of the tx_081 odd-moment no-go ('third moment helps only with lambda_max = O(1)') to the obstruction-evasion table with a real evasion — concretely, either exhibit a Poisson/functional-equation rigidity for Re(u^T P^2 u) analogous to the (verified) trace-asymmetry rigidity, or restate rank_trace_cubic with a remainder that explicitly carries the tr(P^2 Q) overlap term and show the LP dual still clears the gate with that term priced adversarially. 3) FIX THE M1 LP DATA CLASS: rows must span only the achievable product-kernel cone Phi_a x Phi_b x Phi_c (this is where mixed windows genuinely earn their keep) with tolerances propagated from the theorem's error terms; re-anchor the 0.02 decision gate there. Report both p0^(3)-pointwise (upper bound on the upgrade's worth) and p0^(3)-achievable (honest value). 4) HARDEN NUMERICS (B) FROM TYPICAL TO ADVERSARIAL: add the specific stress family from finding 1 — intermediate-depth pairs (X^y ~ polylog, K ~ N/polylog of them) with ordinates micro-shifted by ~pi/(lambda l) to phase-tune Phi at complex argument, on top of an admissible log-density cluster — and require the measured worst-case interaction penalty as an LP row before any M3 proof attempt. 5) FIX THE 7.5(g) CITATION (direction mismatch) and demote the M4 stretch goal (certified value above 0.6818287) to conditional-on-Lemma-C. 6) KEEP AND FOREGROUND THE ROBUST DELIVERABLES: the pair-only LP dual at N=128 (the 0.6725->0.6818 gap certificate, verifiable in the existing Lean Stability harness) and the M5 formal multilinear ceiling are valuable regardless of Lemma C's fate and should be promoted from by-products to primary milestones.

findings.claim: The central mechanism is vacuous: a Schatten-3 tail bound with ANY divergent cutoff V0(T) -> infinity (polylog, polyloglog, anything) gives the cubic row zero asymptotic separating power. An explicit admissible adversary configuration satisfies every row of the Step 4/Step 5 system at both bandwidths while keeping N_d = 5/6 N + o(N), so the joint two-bandwidth LP cannot certify delta_0 > 0. The claimed evasion of the paper's odd-moment no-go (section 7.5(e)) fails because the no-go's proof needs only 'mass at height h -> infinity' along ANY sequence, and h = V0(T)/2 -> infinity is exactly such a sequence.
findings.argument: The no-go (transcript p. 80-81, verified verbatim in tx_081.txt lines 50-56) proves that given (m1, m2), any prescribed m3 is reachable 'by putting mass eps at height h -> infinity (which feeds m3 and nothing else)'. The proposal claims a cutoff V0 = (loglog T)^3 evades this by bounding the spectral support. It does not, because the adversary sits just below the cutoff. CONSTRUCTION (cluster-garnish adversary): take the lemmaR_tight extremal configuration, 2/3 N GUE-positioned simple on-line zeros + 1/6 N tight off-line pairs (cubic charge 0, exactly the configuration the cubic row is supposed to kill), and add k = Delta*N/h0^3 'garnish' clusters, each consisting of h0 = V0/2 = (loglog T)^3/2 SIMPLE on-line zeros packed within one lambda'-resolution cell 1/L' (equivalently, multiplicity-h0 zeros; the cluster version is stronger since at lambda = 1 resolution 1/l the clusters resolve into ordinary simples and pay no k_c multiplicity price). Delta is tuned so the lambda'-cubic equality tr G'^3 = c_3(lambda')N is hit exactly; the doubles-vs-pairs swing is Delta ~ 8*(1/6) = 4/3. AUDIT OF EVERY ROW: (a) lambda' trace: garnish adds k*h0 = Delta*N/h0^2 = o(N) -- absorbed in the (1+o(1)). (b) lambda' Frobenius equality kappa(lambda')N: adds k*h0^2 = Delta*N/h0 = o(N). (c) cubic equality: matched by construction of Delta. (d) tail row Sum_{|lambda_i| >= V0} |lambda_i|^3 = o(N): garnish eigenvalues sit at h0 = V0/2 < V0, contribute ZERO. (e) count ledger of Theorem 1(ii), stated only for V >= (loglog T)^3 = V0: garnish invisible. (f) sign-split rows, power-mean, n_- <= p: garnish eigenvalues are positive, untouched. (g) lambda = 1 counting rows (tr, Frobenius/form-factor near-CUE, inertia, rank-trace k_c): garnish adds o(N) to trace and zero count; its pair-correlation perturbation is k*h0^2 = Delta*N/h0 = o(N) ordered close pairs, an o(1) perturbation of the form factor; marks are all 1 (simples). (h) distinct count: garnish adds k*h0 = o(N) zeros and equal distinct, so N_d/N = 5/6 + o(1). Hence every inequality derivable from the proposed constraint set holds at a configuration with N_d = 5/6 + o(1): delta_0 = 0. LP-DUAL FORM of the same fact: a certificate p(mu) = c1*mu + c2*mu^2 + c3*mu^3 <= 1 on (0, V0] with c3 > 0 forces c3 <= |c2|/V0 (else p(V0) > 1), so cubic leverage decays like 1/V0 -> 0; the proposal's failure-mode-1 mitigation ('only V_0 = polylog is needed') is exactly backwards -- only V0 = O(1), i.e. the full Lindelof-strength lock the proposal admits is out of reach, gives the cubic row nonvanishing force. The garnish is unconditionally admissible: multiplicities/cluster sizes (loglog T)^3 are far below the known m_rho << log|rho| bound and below the ZeroConfig density bound N(t+1)-N(t) << log t, so no unconditional arithmetic input excludes it.

findings.claim: Hidden hardness: repairing the mechanism collapses it onto HL*(4). The only way to price the garnish is an eigenvalue-count ledger n(V) <= C_led * N * V^{-4} enforced down to absolute-constant heights V >= C_abs, and even then the cubic row bites only if 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3 -- a sharp-constant, bulk-height fourth-moment statement that is marginal even with PERFECT constants and is exactly the quartic-equality lever (HL*(4) -> 13/18) already on the program's map. The 'third-moment certificate' is HL*(4) in disguise or nothing.
findings.argument: If the certificate enforces the V^{-4} ledger at all V >= C_abs (the proposal's proof supports this via Chebyshev; the stated theorem restricts to V >= (loglog T)^3, but grant the repair), the garnish at height h must satisfy k <= C_led*N*h^{-4}, capping absorbable cubic mass at Sum_{dyadic h >= C_abs} C_led*N/h ~ 2*C_led*N/C_abs. The row bites iff 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3 (the doubles-vs-pairs swing). Constants: C_led inherits the bridge constant c (eigenvalue V forces window mass >= c*V*l) raised to the MINUS FOURTH power through Chebyshev, times Schur-test band sums for a C^5 taper, times the Gallagher conversion; realistically C_led >= 10^3, making the condition fail by orders of magnitude. Even at the information-theoretic optimum: the true matrix's own fourth moment is m_4(1) = 13/4, so a perfect ledger permits n(3) ~ (13/4)/81 * N ~ 0.04N eigenvalues at height 3, i.e. cubic capacity ~ 1.08N -- already about the full 4/3 swing. Contrast: the quartic EQUALITY Sum lambda_i^4 = (13/4)N (i.e. HL*(4)) does pin everything -- the garnish at h = 3 adds Delta*N*h = 4N of quartic mass (catastrophic violation), and the tight-pair configuration itself costs 32/6 N > 13/4 N. So the discriminating power the proposal attributes to (cubic + polylog tail) actually resides entirely in quartic-equality-strength control, which the proposal explicitly disclaims ('sharpening ... is HL*(4), which we do not assume') and which map-hooks already lists as the known conjecture-to-constant hook (13/18). The route's first substantive certificate step, made sound, is a known-hard conjecture in disguise -- the campaign's recurring failure pattern.

findings.claim: The M2/N4 decision gate is unsound as specified: rerunning the 256-law LP with marks in {1,2} plus a cubic row cannot detect the absorption channel, so a 'ceiling broken / direction live' gate result would be an artifact of the truncated adversary class.
findings.argument: The finding-1 adversary lives in configurations with cluster/multiplicity marks up to h0 = V0/2 -> infinity (or h0 ~ C_led in the repaired O(1)-ledger version). The N4 experiment as specified ('marks {1,2}, pair-correlation rows near-CUE as in the repo, PLUS the cubic row ... at N = 64') excludes these by construction, and N3's demand computation uses the fixed extremal configuration (2/3 simple + 1/6 doubles) only. An LP over an adversary class that omits the absorbing configurations can only overestimate the certificate's power; the gate can fire 'live' when the true asymptotic answer is provably 'dead' (finding 1). To be sound, the LP's mark alphabet must extend to ~V0, which for the proposed divergent cutoff is unbounded in T -- destroying the 'finite, cheap, decision-relevant' character of the milestone. The proposal's own failure-mode 4 gestures at this ('sine-process clustering exactly saturates the cubic row') but misclassifies a provable structural fact as an empirical uncertainty to be 'measured first' by N3/N5.

findings.claim: Support-arithmetic error in the AH/bandwidth evasion: the third trace at bandwidth lambda' carries data of total Fourier support (k-1)*lambda' = 2*lambda' = 1 + O(loglog T/log T), not '3*lambda' ~ 3/2' as the proposal claims. The new arithmetic content beyond bandwidth one is an o(1)-width sliver, not half a unit of new support.
findings.argument: The campaign record (tx_081.txt, verified: 'a Rudnick-Sarnak-type smooth k-correlation statistic whose Fourier support, in Montgomery's alpha-units, reaches Sum_j |xi_j| = k*lambda for k even and (k-1)*lambda for k odd') gives the odd-moment support as (k-1)*lambda; for k = 3 at lambda' = 1/2 + theta*loglog/log this is 1 + 2*theta*loglog/log -> 1. The proposal's evasion of the Alternative-Hypothesis obstruction rests verbatim on 'combined Fourier support 3*lambda' ~ 3/2 > 1, exactly the data class that distinguishes worlds' -- overstated by the full margin. Whether a 3-point functional at total support 1 + o(1) distinguishes the AH law or the 256-law from GUE by Theta(1) is exactly what should have been argued and was not; the distinguishing capacity plausibly degrades continuously as support -> 1+. The formal ceiling-scope evasion (higher-correlation functionals are outside the PairCeiling class) survives -- that claim is verified against lean:ceiling's limitations list -- but the quantitative story sold with it is wrong.

findings.claim: The Step-2 tail assembly is garbled: the displayed bound T_3(V0) << N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}) evaluated at V0 = T^{2lambda-1} is NOT o(N) (first term = N T^eps, second term = N T^{3-5lambda+eps} >> N for lambda < 3/5), and the stated justification '2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0' does not support the claim as written. The fixed-lambda conclusion (cutoff T^{2lambda-1+eps} with decay T^{-delta}) is salvageable by the correct min-ledger assembly, but the mechanism text's derivation is wrong.
findings.argument: The Huxley term must be evaluated only from the crossover V_Hux where Huxley beats the lossy fourth moment: X V^{-6} <= T^{2lambda-1} V^{-4} iff V >= T^{(1-lambda)/2}. Correct assembly: T_3(V0) << N T^eps [ T^{2lambda-1}/V0 + T^{(5lambda-3)/2} ]; the second term is o(N) iff lambda < 3/5, and the first requires V0 >= T^{2lambda-1+delta} with delta > eps. So Theorem 1(i)'s 'in particular' clause survives, but the proposal's own formula at its own operating value contradicts its own o(N) claim -- a referee-level red flag about the care level of the ledger computations, in a proposal whose surviving value is precisely a constants-sensitive ledger.

findings.claim: The advertised zero-density corollary is strictly weaker than 85-year-old results. The cutoff T^{2lambda-1+eps} at fixed lambda in (1/2, 3/5) detects only zeros with |beta - 1/2| >= (2lambda-1+eps)/(2lambda), a CONSTANT distance from the critical line (e.g. >= 0.09 at lambda = 0.55), where Ingham 1940 / Huxley 1972 zero-density already gives N(sigma, T) << T^{c(sigma)} with c(sigma) < 1 -- as strong or stronger than the claimed 'at most N T^{-delta} zeros'.
findings.argument: Eigenvalue X^u >= T^{2lambda-1+eps} with u = |2beta-1| means |beta-1/2| >= (2lambda-1+eps)/(2lambda), a fixed positive distance. At sigma = 0.59, Guth-Maynard gives N(sigma,T) << T^{30(1-sigma)/13} = T^{0.946} and classical bounds are similar; at the lambda = 0.55 threshold's actual distances the corollary offers nothing beyond Ingham's N(sigma,T) << T^{3(1-sigma)/(2-sigma)}. The proposal flags the corollary as conditional on the visibility lemma but sells it as a payoff ('the visibility lemma alone gives the zero-density corollary'); it is not a payoff at all. Relatedly, the headline 'Lindelof lock demoted' conflates regimes: at lambda' = 1/2 + o(1) the polynomial satisfies X^2 <= T polylog, i.e. the trivially-classical fourth-moment regime where the lock was never hard; at every fixed lambda > 1/2 -- the regime the paper's Remark 7.1(ii)/7.5(e) actually concerns -- the cutoff remains a power of T and the moderate-deviation gap remains exactly as open as before (the proposal concedes this in M5: exponent 2 available vs 3+delta needed).

verdicts.repairs: Three salvage paths, in decreasing value. (1) Reposition Theorem 1 honestly: it is plausibly true, provable with 1970s inputs, and is the first spectral-tail statement for this matrix -- but its correct consumers are ones for which a DIVERGENT cutoff suffices, not the cubic LP. The natural candidate: partial orthonormalization. #{|lambda_i| >= V0} << N V0^{-4} = o(N) bad directions means the Gabor family can be orthonormalized off an o(N)-dimensional exceptional subspace; investigate whether the Christoffel-function count at lambda <= 1 tolerates o(N) uncontrolled directions (rank-perturbation bookkeeping is already in RHLinalg). That would be a genuine new instrument, unlike the cubic row. (2) If the cubic direction is kept at all, replace the polylog-cutoff tail row by the all-heights ledger n(V) <= C_led N V^{-4} for V >= C_abs with EXPLICIT constants, and run the M2 LP with mark/cluster alphabet up to the enforced ceiling height (not {1,2}) -- then the LP will honestly report the absorption; my finding-1/finding-2 analysis predicts the answer (dead unless 2*C_led/C_abs < 4/3, unreachable through a Schur-test bridge whose constant enters as c^{-4}), so the cheap first deliverable is the NO-GO paper: 'cubic rows with divergent spectral cutoff are unconditionally absorbed' -- provable today by the cluster-garnish construction, no LP run needed. This is a real, formalizable extension of the ceiling library and pre-empts anyone else's version of this idea. (3) Re-aim the analytic effort at the row that actually pins the garnish: partial quartic control. Any proven range of HL*(4) (restricted shifts |h| <= X^2/T with X^2/T = polylog is a LOGARITHMIC shift range at the near-critical point -- a far weaker statement than full HL*(4) and worth checking against Goldston-Montgomery/Montgomery-Soundararajan averaged results) enters the existing 13/18 machinery directly. The near-critical observation that X^2/T = (log T)^{2theta} shrinks the needed shift range to polylog is the one genuinely promising insight buried in this proposal, and it belongs to the quartic program, not the cubic one. M5 (MD(lambda, delta)) can stand alone as a community target but should be stated without the certificate payoff claims, which finding 1 removes.
literature_flags: Huxley 1972 large-values theorem: the proposal's form R << (G N V^{-2} + G^3 N T V^{-6}) log^C is self-flagged and must be checked against Iwaniec-Kowalski Thm 9.15 / ANTEDB before any of Step 2(iii) or the fixed-lambda Schatten cutoff is trusted; the Theorem 1(i) exponents depend on it.

Rudnick-Sarnak k=3 admissibility range: the transcript (tx_081) states (k-1)*lambda < 2 i.e. lambda < 1 for the third moment (off-diagonal killed iff X^{k/2} << T gives lambda < 2/3), while the proposal cites v5 section 7.2(e) as lambda < 2/3; the proposal uses the conservative range so this is safe, but the v5 statement and the uniformity of the section-5 diagonal method in the X = T^{1/2} polylog window (self-flagged by the proposal) both need verification.

m_3(1) = 2 (sine-kernel third moment of the Gram spectrum at bandwidth one) and the claimed conditional cubic-weight LP value N_d >= 0.85082 under RH: consistent with map-hooks' section 7.5(g) summary but not independently verified; the Step-5 arithmetic '2*m_2 - m_3 = 2*(4/3) - 2 = 2/3' depends on it.

The claim that the paper's Prop 4.1 gives n_- <= p with pair blocks exactly hyperbolic: transcript tx_082 records pair eigenvalues m*L^2*a*(1 +/- A), i.e. generically ASYMMETRIC, so 'pair cubic charge = 0' is exact only in the tight-pair limit -- the proposal's sign-split table should be checked against the actual Prop 4.1 block spectrum.

BGSTB24 = arXiv:2306.04799 stopping at the second moment, and Remark 7.1(ii)/7.5(e) as the paper's statements of the orthonormalization/odd-moment blocks: verified consistent with the campaign record; Gallagher-lemma constants for 1/L-spacing self-flagged by the proposal and load-bearing for the bridge constant c that enters the ledger as c^{-4}.

findings.claim: Theorem 1(i) — the fixed-lambda 'effective spectral cutoff at T^{2lambda-1+eps}' — is false as displayed: the proposal's own assembled bound evaluates to >> N at its own choice of V0, and the correct assembly leaves an N*T^{eps} (or T*polylog) Huxley-zone term that is never o(N) without an unverified log-power condition.
findings.argument: The displayed bound is T_3(V0) <<_eps N T^eps (T^{2lambda-1} V0^{-1} + X V0^{-3}). At the stated operating choice V0 = T^{2lambda-1} with lambda in (1/2, 3/5), the second term is X V0^{-3} = T^{lambda - 3(2lambda-1)} = T^{3-5lambda}, a POSITIVE power of T for lambda < 3/5 (T^{0.40} at lambda=0.52, T^{0.25} at lambda=0.55, T^{0.10} at lambda=0.58 — verified numerically). So the proposal's own formula gives T_3 >> N, contradicting its 'this is o(N)' and the 'In particular ... << N T^{-delta(lambda,eps)}' clause. The proposal's justification '2lambda-1-lambda/3 < 0' only observes that V0 = T^{2lambda-1} < X^{1/3} = T^{lambda/3} for lambda < 3/5 — but that means the Huxley bound (which beats V^{-3} only for V >= X^{1/3}) has NOT yet taken over at V0, so the dyadic assembly splits: (a) V in [V0, X^{1/3}] uses the fourth-moment ladder, contributing ~ N T^{2lambda-1}/V0 (fine if one takes V0 = T^{2lambda-1+eps}, giving N T^{-eps}); (b) V >= X^{1/3} uses Huxley, contributing Sum_dyadic V^3 * n(V) with n(V) ~ G^3 N' T V_B^{-6} log^C = X T V^{-6} * lambda^3 l^{-3} log^C, whose dyadic sum is dominated by V ~ X^{1/3}: X*T*X^{-1} * l^{C-3} = T * l^{C-3}. Since N = T*l/2pi, this is o(N) iff the net log power C < 4 — an exact-constant question in Huxley's theorem (IK Thm 9.15) that the proposal flags as unverified; with the proposal's own coarser stated form n(V) << N T^eps X V^{-6}, the zone contributes N T^eps, which is NOT o(N) and certainly not N T^{-delta}. Consequences: the headline fixed-lambda tail theorem, the quantitative zero-density corollary, and the 'lambda -> 3/5 horizon' narrative all overstate what the displayed inputs deliver. The near-critical part (ii) is NOT hit by this finding (it avoids Huxley entirely) — but part (i) as stated is wrong and must be deleted or downgraded to a polylog-loss statement contingent on Huxley's exact log exponent.

findings.claim: The bridge lemma's additive error term O(T^{1/2} l), being V-independent as stated, makes BOTH parts (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1 non-sequiturs: it licenses cubic tail mass ~ T^{5/4} l >> N = T l at the top of the spectrum, and every downstream capacity argument rests on the ladder holding up to lambda_max.
findings.argument: Theorem 1(0) states #{i: |lambda_i| >= CV} <= C L |{tau: smoothed mass >= cVl}| + O(T^{1/2} l) with the additive term independent of V. The maximal eigenvalue is a priori lambda_max ~ X^{1/2} polylog = T^{lambda/2} polylog (Schur bound via sup|A| <= 2 sqrt(X); equivalently a depth-1/2 off-line pair contributes ~ X^{1/2}). Assembling T_3(V0) = Sum_dyadic V^3 #{lambda_i in [V,2V)} with the stated count, the additive floor contributes at the top level V ~ lambda_max: (T^{lambda/2})^3 * T^{1/2} l = T^{3lambda/2 + 1/2} l, which at lambda = 1/2+ is T^{5/4} l — exceeding N = T l by T^{1/4} (and worse at larger lambda; verified numerically). The Frobenius bound cannot rescue it: Sum_{>=W}|lambda|^3 <= lambda_max * kappa N via Frobenius alone, which is the very divergence the theorem exists to beat. So the proof sketch proves neither (i) nor (ii): the Schatten-3 conclusion requires a V-DEPENDENT error (or a proof that the error term's eigenvalues are bounded), which the sketch does not contain and which is nontrivial precisely at large V where the Prop 4.2 tail factors X^{1/2} = T^{lambda/2} live. This is repairable in principle (edge-window excision, rank bookkeeping with V-dependent thresholds), but it is the single load-bearing analytic gap: findings 4's 'clean ladder at all V up to lambda_max' — the only thing that gives the cubic row any asymptotic bite — is exactly what this hole leaves unproven.

findings.claim: The unconditional cubic budget c_3(lambda') contains asymptotically ZERO triple-correlation information — the genuinely cubic prime resonance is an absolute constant (~2.316) contributing o(N) — so the row's arithmetic input is bandwidth-one pair-correlation data, and the proposal's Alternative-Hypothesis evasion ('consumes triple-correlation data at combined Fourier support 3lambda' ~ 3/2, exactly the data class that distinguishes worlds') is false as an information claim.
findings.argument: Expand the prime side of tr G-hat'^3 in powers of the prime term P: (delta + P)^3 gives delta^3 (mean density geometry), delta*P^2 (a pair-type diagonal reading Sum Lambda(n)^2/n ~ L^2/2, i.e. the form factor F(alpha) on the band, exactly the data class tr^2 already reads with a different weight), and the genuinely cubic P^3 resonance n1*n2 = n3 over prime powers <= X. By unique factorization, n1 n2 = n3 with all three prime powers forces the SAME prime: p^a * p^b = p^{a+b}. Its total mass is Sum_p (log p)^3 Sum_{a,b>=1} p^{-(a+b)} = Sum_p (log p)^3/(p-1)^2 = 2.3158... — an absolute constant (computed numerically over primes to 3*10^6), versus the pair diagonal L^2/2 -> infinity. In the units where tr G-hat = N, this contributes O(N/l^3) = o(N). Off-diagonal near-resonances |log(n1 n2 / n3)| small are exactly what MV BOUNDS (never evaluates) inside the RS range X^3 <= T^{2-eps}, so they enter only as o(N) error. The zero-side pair part of the cubic reads F up to support 2lambda' = 1 + 2 theta loglog/log, but the weight mass on the sliver (1, 2lambda'] is O(loglog/l), i.e. o(N)-irrelevant. CONCLUSION: c_3(lambda') = [density term] + [F(alpha) on |alpha| <= 1 against an explicit weight] + o(N) — pure bandwidth-one pair data. Three consequences. (a) The AH evasion bullet is wrong: no world-distinguishing data class is consumed; any adversarial law matching zeta's band-1 pair data automatically reproduces the budget's VALUE, and pair-data-consistent worlds (AH-type laws included) remain fully relevant adversaries. (b) The only genuinely new content is the NONLINEAR (cubic-spectral) reading of the same data plus the count ladder — 'a nonlinear functional of bandwidth-one pair data', morally adjacent to the ceiling-covered class even though formally outside the Lean theorem's linear format. (c) The adversary's 3-point structure in the support hexagon is a free knob that NO consumed input constrains (only point-process realizability does): the equality row 'config's Sum lambda^3 = c_3 N' asks the adversary to tune one scalar with an infinite-dimensional position freedom. The proposal's honest prior already concedes budget = demand exactly at lambda = 1 (2 = 2); this finding removes the stated reason to hope lambda' near 1/2 is different.

findings.claim: The M2 decision gate is unsound as specified (marks {1,2} + CUE-sampled moments, no capacity row), and a sprinkling adversary shows the cubic row is asymptotically VACUOUS at theta >= 1 and retains bite at theta < 1 only through an LP-with-marks-up-to-W plus an O(N/W) fuzz row — i.e. the odd-moment no-go is evaded not by 'tail bound + sign' as claimed but only by the clean V^{-4} count ladder, which rests on the unproven bridge (finding 2).
findings.argument: Capacity analysis. Given the count ladder n(V) <= c(T) N V^{-4}, an adversary can shift the cubic equality row by adding on-line clusters of multiplicity m (positive shift) or deep-pair clusters (negative shift, costing nothing at lambda' since no inertia rows run there) at density n: cubic shift n*m^3, Frobenius/pair-row cost n*m^2, trace cost n*m, objective cost n. (I) At theta >= 1 the slice loss makes c(T) >= (loglog T)^2 (the proposal's own n_1 bound), and the choice m = loglog T, n = eps N/m^2 with eps = 1/sqrt(loglog T) satisfies the count row (eps <= (loglog)^2/m^2, verified numerically), costs eps*N = o(N) in Frobenius and pair rows, o(N) in trace and objective, stays below the V0 = (loglog)^3 tail cutoff — and swings the cubic row by eps*N*m = N*sqrt(loglog T) -> unboundedly more than the Theta(N) double-vs-pair signal. The cubic row at theta >= 1 is therefore satisfiable/neutralizable at asymptotically zero cost: the §7.5(e) no-go ('mass at height h -> infinity feeds m_3 freely') reasserts itself because V0 -> infinity is 'unbounded support' in the only sense that matters (per-unit-cubic cost at height V0 is 1/V0 -> 0). Theorem 1(ii)'s theta > 1 branch is decorative and the (loglog)^3-cutoff headline is a red herring. (II) At theta < 1 strictly, the slice loss (log T)^{2theta-2}(loglog)^2 = o(1), the ladder is clean (c(T) = O(1)), and the total cubic capacity from mark scales >= W is Sum_dyadic m^3 * c N m^{-4} ~ 2cN/W -> so the row CAN retain Theta(N) bite modulo an O(N/W) fuzz — this is the correct, narrower version of the evasion, and it is contingent on finding 2's bridge repair holding at ALL V. (III) Gate unsoundness: the specified N4 rerun of the 256-law LP with marks {1,2} forbids exactly the mark-m sprinkling the true asymptotic adversary is allowed — a 'ceiling break' outcome can be a pure artifact of the mark cap (false positive); conversely without the O(N/W) fuzz row a finite-N 'bites' outcome does not survive T -> infinity. And N3's CUE-sampling hard-codes GUE triple-correlation structure the adversary is not bound by (finding 3c). The gate must be re-specified: marks up to W, an explicit capacity/fuzz row, adversarial 3-point freedom subject only to realizability. Expected direction of the corrected computation, given finding 3 and the designer's own 2=2 admission: absorption, i.e. the no-go branch.

findings.claim: The sign-split discrimination (tight pair charges 4 units of negative Frobenius mass, double charges 0) is a per-isolated-block statement that fails under adversarial clustering: PSD on-line mass lifts a pair's negative eigenvalue toward 0 (annihilation), Sylvester gives only n_- <= p (never a lower bound), and the needed visibility lemma is the same configuration-free visibility theorem the campaign record argues is impossible — so Step 4's 'different corners of the constraint polytope' smear back together against the worst-case adversary.
findings.argument: The Step 4 separation requires reading, from the spectrum of G-hat', that a tight off-line pair contributes negative mass ~4 while an on-line double contributes none. But the matrix is a SUM of blocks: adding a PSD block (on-line cluster) to a hyperbolic pair block can only raise eigenvalues (Weyl), so an adversary placing each tight pair inside an on-line cluster drives its negative eigenvalue toward or past 0 — the campaign's own measurements found the honest compressed index identically 0 for X = 10^2..10^6 while sign-based predictions gave hundreds, and Part I argues (uncertainty-principle heuristic, empirical annihilation laws L*_ann) that no configuration-free visibility theorem exists. The certificate must be valid configuration-by-configuration, i.e. against the clustered presentation; then the only unconditional rows left are n_-(G') <= p and the global moment equalities. The proposal half-concedes this (M3b listed as 'the genuinely hard new mathematics'; failure mode 3's fallback drops the visibility lemma) but does not follow the concession to its conclusion: in the fallback, the negative-spectrum rows (Sum_-|lambda|^3 <= V0 Sum_- lambda^2, power-mean, n_- <= p) are correct linear algebra but toothless for the double-vs-pair separation, because the adversary's pair-rich configuration simply presents with Sum_- ~ 0 — indistinguishable in every surviving row from the double-rich configuration except through the cubic equality, which is finding 3+4's one nonlinear scalar of bandwidth-one pair data with O(N/W) fuzz. The lemmaR_tight degeneracy is therefore NOT broken by anything currently provable in the proposal; at best it is dented by the repaired M2 LP, whose outcome is genuinely open but adversely indicated.

findings.claim: Assorted smaller defects: the bridge 'converse' direction is unproven (signed-vs-absolute smoothing), Theorem 1(ii)'s count-bound threshold is inconsistent with its own ledger, and numerics N1 cannot distinguish the predicted regimes at accessible heights.
findings.argument: (a) Theorem 1(0)'s converse ('every such tau lies within O(1/L) of a window supporting an eigenvalue >= cV/C') does not follow from the Rayleigh argument: the diagonal entry G_kk is the SIGNED phi-hat-smoothed integral, while the ledger controls smoothed |A|; A has band L, so it can rotate a full phase period within one 2pi/L window and partially cancel. Harmless for the tail theorem (only the forward direction is used) but stated as part of the theorem. (b) The count bound in (ii) is stated 'for all V >= (loglog T)^3', yet the Chebyshev ledger proves it for all V >= C — and finding 4 shows the range below (loglog)^3 is where the leverage battle actually happens; the statement should claim what the proof gives. (c) N1 proposes T = 10^5..10^6 to validate tail exponents and falsify via 'stable slope -2'; but at T <= 10^6, (loglog T)^3 ~ 17 while lambda_max ~ T^{1/4} ~ 18-32 — the cutoff scale and the top of the spectrum coincide, so the asymptotic regimes the prediction separates are not resolved at accessible heights (consistent with the map's warning that all finite-T certificate quantities are far from asymptotic). N1 as designed can neither validate nor falsify the mechanism. (d) For balance: I verified the free fourth-moment diagonal Sum(Lambda*Lambda)(m)^2/m = 2(Sum Lambda^2/n)^2(1+o(1)) = L^4/2 (unique-factorization argument is correct, same-prime coincidences are O(1)), the slice variance v_1 = theta*l*loglog T, the n_1 slice bound, the power-mean and Frobenius-split rows, and the dimension-cap and kappa evasions (counting only at lambda = 1) — these parts are sound.

(2) Delete Theorem 1(i)'s 'In particular' clause or downgrade it to a polylog-loss statement conditional on the exact log power in Huxley's theorem (o(N) requires net log power < 4 in my accounting; the T^eps form never suffices); drop the quantitative fixed-lambda zero-density corollary accordingly. (3) Fix the operating regime to theta < 1 strictly and state that theta >= 1 has no certificate value (sprinkling adversary). (4) Re-specify the M2 gate before trusting it in either direction: exact-rational LP with marks up to W, an explicit O(N/W) cubic-capacity fuzz row derived from the repaired ladder, adversarial triple-correlation freedom subject only to point-process realizability (not CUE sampling), and the sign-split rows evaluated on clustered/annihilated presentations. Only that LP is decision-relevant; a break in the marks-{1,2} rerun is not evidence. (5) Reframe the claims honestly: the route is 'a nonlinear spectral reading of bandwidth-one pair-correlation data with quantitative high-spectrum capacity control', not 'unconditional consumption of triple correlation'; strike the AH data-class bullet. (6) Keep and foreground the genuinely defensible deliverables: repaired Theorem 1(ii) as a standalone first-of-its-kind spectral-tail statement, the MD(lambda, delta) problem statement for the large-values community, and the sharpened no-go publication if the corrected M2 shows absorption — the proposal's own pricing of that branch is its most robust feature.
